screening_results.reason: Excluded because the study does not present or regulate emotional VISUAL stimuli (I7 not met). The fMRI task instructed emotion-introspection (a mindfulness/awareness strategy) and reports within-task contrasts (feel>think, feel>neutral) and whole-brain group analyses, but these contrasts reflect self-focused regulation from baseline without emotionally-valenced visual stimuli; only neutral pictures were used as distractors. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion-regulation-like strategy: emotion-introspection), I8 (clinical sample qualifies), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses), I11 (results described in text/supplement). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (emotional stimuli are VISUAL — not satisfied). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed explicit emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal: downregulate negative, upregulate positive) using visual stimuli (emotional pictures). It reports within-task contrasts (negative-downregulate > attend, positive-upregulate > attend, attend > baseline) and performs voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (FSL Randomise permutation tests) in standard (MNI) space, with results described as clusters/regions and figures/tables. A healthy control group is reported alongside the clinical rrMDD group. Full article text (methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs cognitive reappraisal during an emotion-regulation task (regulate > experience; I6). Emotional stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). The sample includes gambling disorder patients and healthy controls with group-level results reported separately (I8). The report includes within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g. ‘regulate’ > ‘experience’) and behavioural emotion-reduction scores (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates in MNI space and cluster-thresholding details (e.g. peak MNI x=-60,y=20,Z=32; thresholding and cluster sizes described), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria apply: this is empirical fMRI activation (not review), reports whole-brain activations (not ROI-only), includes within-group task effects (not only between-group), and is not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (distancing, a form of cognitive reappraisal) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The sample includes a clinical group (PMDD) and healthy controls with results reported for groups separately. Analyses include within-task regulation contrasts (negative, far > negative, close) and unregulated contrasts (negative > neutral). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise group analyses with peak coordinates (MNI) and cluster-corrected results. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

The study is excluded because the emotional stimuli that participants regulated were non-visual (auditory vignettes and spoken negative self-belief statements presented while participants had eyes closed). This fails inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be VISUAL). Relevant inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: reappraisal and acceptance), I8 (sample acceptable; patient and control groups reported), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported, e.g., reappraise > react, accept > react), I10 (whole-brain group-level analyses with corrected statistical maps), and I11 (results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that clearly meets all inclusion criteria: it uses an instructed cognitive emotion regulation paradigm (increase/decrease vs view) during fMRI (I6), with visual stimuli (static face photographs; I7), includes patient and matched control groups reported separately (I8), and reports within-task regulation contrasts ([increase+decrease] > view) behaviorally and neurally (I9). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported with cluster-corrected results and tables/coordinates (I10,I11). Methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. The study is therefore eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of instructed visual emotion regulation fMRI studies.

Full text reports an event-related task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal (decrease cue) with visual stimuli (IAPS images). It includes within-task contrasts relevant to the review (decrease > look negative; look negative > look neutral), reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-corrected results and peak coordinates described, and includes both clinical (SI) and control groups with separate comparisons. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because its emotional stimuli are words (visual word stimuli), which the review's criteria explicitly exclude (I7 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (eligible sample: non-clinical groups reported separately), I9 (reports within-task contrast: unpleasant > neutral), I10 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates), and I11 (results described in text/tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal/acceptance; participants were instructed to respond to ink color and ignore word meaning rather than to regulate emotion) and I7 (stimuli are words/sentences, which are excluded by the meta-analysis). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) applicable. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal: ‘regulate’ vs ‘attend’), using visual stimuli (neutral, fear, and OCD-related pictures). It reports within-task regulation contrasts (fear_regulate > attend; OCD_regulate > attend) and unregulated viewing contrasts (fear > neutral; OCD > neutral). The sample includes patients, unaffected siblings, and healthy controls with control-group results reported separately. Although ROI analyses are emphasized, the manuscript references supplemental whole-brain results and reports voxelwise SPM analyses (group-level contrasts), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, peak-coordinate results in standard space (supplementary materials). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs a cognitive emotion regulation strategy ('reality check' reappraisal) with visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures; transfer video clips). The authors report within-task contrasts related to regulation (regulate > view; regulate > baseline; view > baseline) and conduct group-level whole-brain analyses (voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not non-empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group task effects, and is not an empathy/perspective-taking-only study).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to engage in a self-referential emotion regulation strategy (imagining/engaging oneself in positive-social scenes), using visual stimuli (IAPS/NAPS/GAPED images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (regulation > viewing; positive > neutral; interaction), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and FWE correction, and full methods/results/discussion. All inclusion criteria relevant to the review are met and none of the exclusion criteria apply (the study is not non-empirical, does not report only ROI or connectivity-only results, and includes within-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete. Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal during presentation of visual IAPS images and compares reappraise versus view conditions. The sample includes PTSD patients and healthy controls with group-level results reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise>view), and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (voxel-wise p<.001, cluster-wise pFWE<.05) with reported activation peaks. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The full text reports an original, task-based fMRI study in SAD patients using an instructed cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task (Reappraise vs Look Negative) with visual stimuli (IAPS images). The analysis includes within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraise > Look Negative) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates and corrected cluster thresholds. The methods, results, and discussion are present and sufficient. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-visual stimuli, or non-empirical article). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > attend negative; suppress > attend negative), conducts group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (with FWE cluster correction) and provides peak coordinates; both patient and control groups are included and within-group task effects are reported. All required inclusion criteria are therefore met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This article is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (self-focused reappraisal to increase and decrease negative emotion) during presentation of visual stimuli (angry and neutral faces). It reports within-task contrasts (view-angry > view-neutral; increase > view-angry; decrease > view-angry; within- and between-group contrasts) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster-thresholded maps and tables of activations). The sample includes a clinical group (MDD) and healthy controls with results reported separately. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI study in adolescents that instructed an emotion-regulation strategy (recall of positive autobiographical memories; “try to feel what you felt then”) paired to visual stimuli (happy self-face images), satisfying an instructed regulation manipulation. The stimuli are visual (static face images). The sample includes clinical (depressed) and healthy adolescents. The paper reports within-task contrasts (feedback+self-face > count-backwards+other-face) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses using standard thresholds and reports peak coordinates (e.g., hippocampus [34 −34 −10]; [−36 −26 −14]), fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. The study does not meet exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, not an empathy/perspective-taking-only task). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative affect while viewing visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise Negative > Attend Negative; Attend Negative > Attend Neutral) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. Sample details and task methods are fully described. Although resting-state connectivity analyses are also reported, task activation maps meeting inclusion criteria are clearly provided. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This full-text describes a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed participants to downregulate emotion via distancing (a reappraisal strategy) while viewing visual pictures (negative, positive, neutral). The sample includes acute anorexia nervosa patients and matched healthy controls with separate group analyses. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to the review (negative watch > neutral; negative watch > negative distance; negative watch < negative distance) and provides voxelwise results with peak coordinates in standard space (MNI), including mention of whole-brain/exploratory results (Fig. S1) and reported cluster peaks. Analyses are not limited to ROI/SVC-only results. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion-regulation task (affect labeling vs gender labeling), with visual stimuli (photographs of faces). Sample includes clinical (SAD) and healthy control groups. The paper reports within-task contrasts (affect label > gender label) and pre/post treatment paired analyses, and conducts whole-brain, voxelwise psychophysiological interaction (PPI) analyses with whole-brain correction and reported clusters/coordinates. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; not only connectivity without task activation maps; within-group effects are reported; not an empathy-only task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria: participants were exposed to auditory script-driven imagery (not VISUAL stimuli), and they were instructed to imagine scenes to provoke emotion but were not instructed to use any emotion-regulation strategy. Specifically, inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports within-task contrasts such as anger>baseline and aggression>baseline), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates), and I11 (results reported in text/tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy), I7 (regulated stimuli are not visual). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal using visual stimuli in OCD patients and healthy controls, and it reports within-task contrasts (regulate > maintain) at the ICA component/network level. However, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps for the regulation contrasts with peak coordinates in a standard stereotactic space (the main statistical tests for the key task contrasts are performed on ICA component time-course beta-weights using SPSS rather than voxelwise SPM second-level contrasts with reported coordinates). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map with peak coordinates). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion E4 met: the study reports only ROI-based analyses (average activations from 70 anatomical ROIs used in random forest models) and does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map with peak coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation — cognitive reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli — IAPS images), I8 (sample includes clinical participants; eligible), I9 (within-task conditions/contrasts: maintain and reappraise). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level map reported). The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Because the review requires a whole-brain task activation map (I10) and this paper provides only ROI-based results, it must be excluded under E4.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed cognitive reappraisal (an emotion regulation strategy) while participants viewed visual negative and neutral images (IAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > Look-Negative and Look-Negative > Look-Neutral) and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and FWE-corrected results. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text (not truncated). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I9, I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is empirical (not E3), includes whole-brain activation maps (not only ROI, so not E4), reports activation contrasts (not only connectivity, so not E5), includes within-task effects (not only between-group contrasts, so not E6), and it is not an empathy/perspective-taking study lacking regulation instructions (not E7). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which participants performed an instructed reappraisal task (Reappraise/Decrease vs Look) using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures) and additional face-viewing tasks. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise Negative vs Look Negative) and unregulated viewing (Look Negative vs Neutral). Voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses were conducted and reported (clusters/coordinates referenced in supplemental tables), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Sample (clinical PTSD) is acceptable. Although some ROI analyses are described, whole-brain voxelwise results are also presented. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise-negative) using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The analysis includes within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraise > attend-negative; attend-negative > attend-neutral) and whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (3dMVM; cluster-thresholding with Monte Carlo correction), with results reported in the text and supplementary materials. The sample includes both clinical (BD, SZ) and healthy control groups with separate group-level reporting. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and supplementary tables/figures are referenced for coordinates/details. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This is a task-based fMRI study of fear conditioning/extinction using visual CS (rooms/colored lamps) in ADHD vs controls. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task contrasts, e.g., CS+ vs CS-; extinction contrasts), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis with MNI coordinates), I11 (coordinates and results clearly reported). However the study does NOT instruct an emotion regulation strategy (no cognitive reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other instructed regulation); it examines conditioned fear/extinction without regulation instructions, so I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because it fails to satisfy I6 (instructed emotion regulation).

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed cognitive reappraisal using visual video stimuli with SAD and HC groups (meets I5, I6, I7, I8). However, the paper reports ROI-based connectivity (DEPNA) analyses and behavioral ratings rather than any group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps or peak coordinates. It does not present within-task whole-brain contrasts (e.g., reappraise > watch) or voxelwise tables/figures, so inclusion criteria I9 and I10 are not satisfied. Therefore the study falls under exclusions for reporting only ROI/connectivity analyses without accompanying whole‑brain task activation results (E4, E5). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (and reports the reappraise > attend-negative contrast), uses visual stimuli (IAPS images), includes patient and healthy control groups with separate reporting, and presents within-task contrasts and group-level whole-brain analyses with reported peak coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing complete assessment against the inclusion/exclusion criteria.

Excluded because the study does not meet inclusion criterion I7: emotional stimuli are not visual. The neurofeedback task required participants to recall positive autobiographical memories (an internal/imagery-based emotional induction), not to view or regulate responses to external visual emotional stimuli. Met inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy was used), I9 (within-task contrasts/condition beta for the ‘happy’ neurofeedback blocks were reported and used in analysis), I10 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level mapping with reported peak coordinates), and I11 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Because the meta-analysis specifically targets studies regulating or viewing visual emotional stimuli, this study is not eligible despite meeting several other criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study (n-back) that manipulated emotional state via olfactory stimuli (negative vs neutral) and reports whole-brain group-level activation coordinates. However, the study does not meet key criteria for the review: (1) the emotional stimuli are olfactory (non-visual), not visual images or videos, so I7 is not met; (2) there was no instructed emotion-regulation task (no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or similar instructions), so I6 is not met. The study does meet I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample criteria: includes clinical and control groups reported), I9 (reports within-task emotional contrast negative vs neutral), I10 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps with coordinates), and I11 (results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED because it fails required inclusion criteria I6 and I7.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional face stimuli with patients and controls and reports emotional vs neutral contrasts, but it does not meet the review's requirements for inclusion. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample includes patient and control groups), I9 (reports an unregulated viewing contrast: emotional > neutral). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; task required ignoring emotional expressions rather than instructing reappraisal or other regulation), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-activation peak coordinates are reported in standard space for univariate activation contrasts; the reported peak coordinates pertain to PPI connectivity results). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (the paper reports primarily seed-based/task-dependent connectivity [PPI] results without accompanying whole-brain task activation maps/coordinates). Because E5 is met, the study must be excluded.

Full text meets all inclusion criteria: (I5) task-based fMRI; (I6) instructed emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise condition); (I7) visual stimuli (IAPS pictures, neutral images); (I8) sample includes clinical (GAD) and healthy control groups reported separately; (I9) reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > Look-Neutral; Look-Negative > Look-Neutral); (I10) whole-brain voxel-wise analyses with cluster correction and peak MNI coordinates; (I11) results reported in text/figures. No exclusion criteria are met. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation (accept, worry, suppress) in a clinical GAD sample and reports within-task contrasts and group-level maps. However, the emotional stimuli were personally relevant worry statements presented as text (word/sentence stimuli: “What if…?”), not visual images, videos, or film clips. Inclusion criterion I7 requires regulated stimuli to be VISUAL (e.g., IAPS images, photographs, faces, scenes, or video clips); studies using only word/sentence stimuli are excluded. Therefore the study fails I7 and must be excluded. Other inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation including acceptance), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (within-task contrasts reported), and I10/I11 (group-level whole-brain results/maps are reported/illustrated). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) appear to apply. Full text appears complete.

This full-text reports an event-related, task-based fMRI experiment using an instructed cognitive reappraisal strategy (distancing) with visual IAPS images; includes behavioral and neural within-task contrasts (e.g., distance>baseline, spontaneous_negative>baseline); presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE inference; and reports connectivity and ROI analyses alongside whole-brain maps. The article contains full introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. These elements satisfy all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed an emotion-regulation strategy (distraction via a MEMORIZE vs VIEW paradigm) while presenting visual emotional stimuli (negative and neutral pictures from IAPS/EmoPics). The sample includes a clinical group (BPD patients) and control groups. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., MEMORIZE>VIEW, NEGATIVE>NEUTRAL), performs group- and time-level whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses, and provides peak coordinates and cluster results. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, limitations, refs) is present. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. The full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (face-matching) with a within-task contrast (face-matching > shape-matching) isolating emotional processing. It reports group-level, whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates and includes both a clinical bipolar sample and healthy controls (groups reported separately). Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction (e.g., reappraisal) was given, the meta-analysis objective accepts studies that involve viewing emotional stimuli without regulating. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present; full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual (static scene) stimuli with both SAD and healthy control groups, and it reports within-task contrasts (disorder-related > neutral) and whole-brain analyses. However, participants were not instructed to use any emotion-regulation strategy — the paradigm presented task-irrelevant emotional scenes while subjects performed a feature-based task, with no instruction to reappraise, distance, accept, or otherwise regulate emotional responses. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation task) is not met, so the study must be excluded despite meeting other criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (“Think Positive”/“Think Negative”) while viewing visual stimuli (neutral faces). It reports within-task contrasts (Enhance Positive > Pre-Regulation; Enhance Negative > Pre-Regulation; Either Regulation > Pre-Regulation) and group comparisons with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM results (thresholds and coordinate tables are reported). Sample includes ASD and control groups with results presented separately. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not empathy-without-regulation).

This is a task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were instructed to use cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate emotional responses to visual IAPS images (meets I5–I7). The sample (healthy adults) is acceptable (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (regulate > view) and ROI beta estimates for ‘view’ and ‘regulate’ (I9). A group-level whole-brain GLM and activation foci with Talairach coordinates are reported for the localizer and task (FDR-corrected), satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting (I10–I11). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Therefore the study should be included in the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual stimuli (fear/neutral faces; I7) in an eligible sample (I8). The paper reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (fear > neutral anticipation; I9), includes a voxel-wise whole-brain exploratory analysis with reported peak coordinates (I10, I11). However, participants were not instructed to use any emotion-regulation strategy during the task — emotion regulation was only measured by questionnaire post hoc. The study therefore does NOT meet I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation manipulation). Because the review’s inclusion criteria require an instructed regulation task (I6), I exclude this paper. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met; full text appears complete.

This article meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal Reduce Emotion vs Maintain; I6), used visual stimuli (IAPS negative images; I7), included both clinical (GAD, PD) and healthy control groups reported separately (I8), reported within-task contrasts (Reappraise and Maintain versus Baseline and Reappraise vs Maintain; I9), and conducted whole-brain voxelwise group analyses with cluster thresholds and reported peak coordinates (I10,I11). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Thus the study should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) with visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise>Maintain) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space, and supplementary ROI analyses. The sample includes a clinical PTSD group and a combat-exposed control group with results reported separately. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based (event-related) fMRI study that uses an implicit cognitive reappraisal manipulation (non-negative vs negative descriptions preceding negative images) to modulate emotional responses. Visual stimuli (IAPS pictures) were used. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (NNEG-DESC vs NEG-DESC) and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and corrected cluster results. Participant groups (PD and HC) are reported separately. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11) and none of the exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical issues). Full text is complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI trial using visual food images and reports within-task contrasts (e.g., high-fat/high-sugar food > vegetables; milkshake cue/receipt contrasts) and whole-brain analyses, but it does NOT instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses during the fMRI paradigms (participants were explicitly not asked to apply cognitive reappraisals during scans), so I6 (an instructed regulation task) is not met. Additionally, the provided full text does not report peak coordinates for whole-brain group-level maps needed for coordinate-based meta-analysis (I10 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered by the provided content.

The full text describes a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive regulation strategies (CBT-based long-term thinking; reappraisal) during presentation of visual stimuli (alcohol pictures and IAPS negative/neutral images). It reports within-task regulation contrasts (LATER>NOW; REAPPRAISE-Negative>LOOK-Negative), trial-by-trial parametric analyses, and familywise-error corrected whole-brain group-level results with peak coordinates in MNI space and tables/figures. The sample (individuals with AUD) is an eligible participant group and contrasts are reported at the group level. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; includes whole-brain activation maps; not connectivity-only; reports within-task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (downregulation) during exposure to visual social-exclusion images. The sample (healthy college students) is eligible. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraisal vs no-reappraisal) and whole-brain group-level analyses with MNI peak coordinates and FDR correction; voxel-wise and ROI results are both presented. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, includes activation maps and within-task effects, not an empathy-only task without regulation). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (reappraisal and mental imagery ‘change image’) using visual IAPS pictures and neutral blocks. It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (reappraise > maintain; change image > maintain) and unregulated viewing (maintain > just look). Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise inference with peak coordinates reported (MNI/Talairach) and exploratory whole-brain results in the text/tables. Participant groups (affected, high-risk, low-risk) are reported separately. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion: E5 (study reports only connectivity analyses—multi-region gPPI and network contingency analyses—without reporting any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-activation maps or peak coordinates). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: reappraisal and distraction), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS images), I8 (sample includes clinical groups and controls), I9 (within-task contrasts related to regulation: distraction vs reappraisal, comparisons with passive viewing). Inclusion criteria not met: I10 (no evidence in full text of whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or reported peak coordinates). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I7: the regulated stimuli are not visual emotional images or film clips but a psychosocial stress task (mental arithmetic with time pressure and social-evaluative feedback). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I6 (an instructed cognitive regulation strategy—reappraisal/suppression—was applied), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task contrasts related to regulation and stress reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates), I11 (results/tables clearly described). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text is complete and contains methods, results, and discussion. Because the meta-analysis specifically requires visual emotional stimuli (I7), this study is not eligible despite satisfying other criteria.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the required inclusion criterion I6: there was no instruction to regulate emotion (no reappraisal/distancing/acceptance or other instructed emotion-regulation strategy). (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli - visual cues), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task unregulated contrast: difficult > easy cue/anticipation effects reflecting emotional response), I10 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses in MNI space with reported coordinates), I11 (results reported in text/tables). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation task/contrast such as reappraise > look). Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results and discussion; fulltext_incomplete=false. The study therefore cannot be included because it lacks an instructed emotion-regulation manipulation/contrast required by the protocol.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of instructed cognitive reappraisal using visual stimuli in a mixed clinical/control child sample (meets I5, I6, I7, I8) and it reports within-task contrasts in the form of Reappraise > View Sad PPI analyses (meets I9), the paper reports only seed-based task-related functional connectivity (PPI) results and does not present a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map (with peak coordinates) for activation contrasts. The review’s exclusion E5 applies: studies that report ONLY seed-based/effective connectivity analyses without also reporting whole-brain activation results are excluded. Therefore the study must be excluded from the activation-focused meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > view) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinate tables/figures. The sample includes MDD patients and separate healthy controls. Full methods, results, and discussion are present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text is complete but the study does not meet the key regulation-related inclusion criterion I6. This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual stimuli (I7) with an eligible sample (I8). The paper reports unregulated viewing contrasts (Negative > Neutral) within-task (I9) and presents whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and tables/figures (I10, I11). However, participants performed an emotional oddball attention task and were not instructed to use any emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance); there is no instructed regulation condition or reappraise>view contrast. Therefore I6 is not met, and per the screening rules the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an explicit emotion/craving regulation strategy (proximal/distal distancing), using visual stimuli (video clips). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (close vs. far) and unregulated viewing (smoke vs. non-smoke), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-thresholded Z maps) with referenced anatomical localization and supplementary tables. The sample (young adult smokers) is acceptable. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports within-task effects, and the perspective-taking instruction is explicitly used to modulate craving). Thus the study meets all specified inclusion criteria.

This article reports an original, task-based fMRI experiment (I5) with explicit instructed emotion regulation strategies including cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) and distraction (I6). Emotional stimuli were visual static images (IAPS and internet photos) (I7). Sample (healthy adult females) is eligible (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation and unregulated viewing (e.g., down-regulation > look, up-regulation > look, distraction > look) and associated behavioral correlations (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described and thresholded, with peak coordinates reported in MNI space and supplementary tables/figures (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) with an instructed attentional regulation condition (shape recognition trials requiring shifting attention away from emotional content), and explicit contrasts comparing regulation (SRT) versus emotion recognition (ERT) and valence contrasts. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (FWE cluster-level thresholds) and results reported (with extraction of peak coordinates/ROIs and supplementary material). Patient and control groups are reported separately. Thus all inclusion criteria are met: task-based fMRI (I5), instructed emotion regulation (attentional control) (I6), visual stimuli (I7), appropriate sample with separate control reporting (I8), within-task regulation/viewing contrasts reported (I9), whole-brain group-level analyses (I10) and whole-brain results available in text/supplement (I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion E4 applies: the paper reports ROI-based task activation results (region-of-interest analyses with family-wise error correction) and does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or whole-brain analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—static facial images), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrasts, e.g., negative > happy). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation task during fMRI; passive viewing only), I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise activation map reported), I11 (not applicable because whole-brain results are absent). Because the review requires whole-brain task activation evidence (I10) and studies reporting only ROI/small-volume-corrected results without whole-brain analysis are excluded (E4), this study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (reappraisal and suppression) using visual IAPS pictures, reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > attend negative, attend negative > fixation) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with reported activations and thresholds. The sample includes patients, siblings and a healthy control group with group-level results reported separately. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli, whole-brain group analyses, and within-task emotion contrasts. However, participants were not instructed to use an emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing) and no instructed regulation contrast (e.g., reappraise > watch) is reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (no instructed emotion regulation). All other inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—faces), I8 (participant sample acceptable), I9 (within-task emotion contrasts/unregulated viewing contrasts reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain analysis), and I11 (results described/thresholded). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on failure to meet I6 (instructed emotion regulation).

The full text describes a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (fearful vs calm faces) with a within-task contrast (fearful > calm) and whole-brain group-level analyses with reported peak coordinates. The sample (children, ASD and TD) is acceptable. Although the task did not instruct emotion regulation (participants performed a gender identification task), the meta-analysis objective explicitly allows unregulated viewing contrasts; thus the study satisfies the requirement for an unregulated viewing contrast. Whole-brain results are reported, and supplementary coordinates are available. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation using visual stimuli (I5, I6, I7) with eligible samples (I8) and it reports within-task contrasts (MAINTAIN vs SUPPRESS) and within-group effects (I9), the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or peak coordinates in standard space. Analyses are ROI-based connectivity (195-ROI atlas), network-based statistics and graph-theory metrics (connectivity results), with no accompanying whole-brain activation maps. This violates inclusion criterion I10 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (connectivity-only analyses without whole-brain task activation results). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (DECREASE vs LOOK), uses visual stimuli (IAPS images), reports within-task regulation and reactivity contrasts (e.g., decrease-negative > look-negative; look-negative > look-neutral), and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with reported peak coordinates and tables. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs reappraisal and includes elderly clinical and control samples (I5, I6, I8 satisfied). However, the regulated stimuli are personalized worry scripts presented as sentences (script-driven imagery/word stimuli), not visual images, so I7 (visual stimuli) is not met. More importantly, the paper reports only seed-based task functional connectivity (seed-to-voxel FC) results and does not report any whole-brain task-evoked activation contrasts (e.g., reappraise>look) or voxelwise activation peak coordinates, thus failing I9 and I10 and meeting exclusion E5 (only connectivity analyses). It also lacks within-group task activation effects reported as task contrasts (reappraise>maintain etc.), meeting exclusion E6. Therefore it does not meet all required inclusion criteria and is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation results (main effects of emotion, condition, and contrasts involving emotional > neutral). Although the task (affective Stroop) does not instruct participants to use an explicit emotion-regulation strategy, the meta-analysis objective allows inclusion of studies that involve viewing emotional stimuli without regulation. The study provides whole-brain analyses with coordinates and relevant within-task contrasts (emotion > neutral; view trials), a suitable sample (ADHD and healthy controls reported separately), and results reported in text and supplemental data. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal) using visual stimuli (IAPS images) in combat-exposed veterans with and without PTSD. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise > Maintain; Maintain > Look) and provides group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates and tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, imaging, analysis), Results (behavioral and fMRI), and Discussion. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet all required inclusion criteria. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (the paper reports seed-based PPI connectivity and ROI amygdala analyses but does not provide a group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates in standard space). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—faces), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports within-task contrasts/unregulated viewing contrasts: mother vs stranger and amygdala reactivity). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; participants viewed stimuli and made button presses but were not instructed to regulate emotion), I10 (no clear whole-brain task-evoked statistical map with peak coordinates reported). Full text appears complete for screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is a resting-state fMRI and structural MRI (VBM) study applying multivariate classification to distinguish MDD and BD in medication-free subjects. It does not involve any task-based fMRI with instructed emotion regulation or presentation of visual emotional stimuli, nor does it report within-task emotion-regulation contrasts or whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Therefore it does not meet the core task-based inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal) and a learning-based placebo condition, using visual IAPS pictures as stimuli. The sample is healthy adults. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraisal vs. control; placebo vs. control) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (MNI/Talairach) presented in tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-only design). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs cognitive reappraisal and uses visual stimuli (faces) with within-task contrasts (look vs reappraise), and an eligible sample. However, the reported results focus on an a priori amygdala ROI (ROI-masked analyses and extracted parameter estimates) and do not present a group-level whole-brain, voxelwise statistical map with peak coordinates in standard space. Therefore it meets exclusion E4 (only ROI/SVC results reported) and does not satisfy I10 (whole-brain evidence) nor I11 (coordinate reporting).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive emotion regulation (detachment/reappraisal) while participants view visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It includes both MDD patients and healthy controls with separate group analyses, reports within-task contrasts (e.g., negative regulation > no regulation; negative > neutral), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates and FWE correction. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive emotion regulation (explicit reappraisal) during presentation of visual stimuli (fear and OCD-related pictures). The sample includes both OCD patients and matched healthy controls with group-level results reported separately. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. fear regulate > attend; OCD-related regulate > attend) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space (with ROI and whole-brain reporting). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion regulation paradigm (MAINTAIN, INCREASE, DECREASE) employing cognitive reappraisal strategies with visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (DECREASE > MAINTAIN, INCREASE > MAINTAIN) and unregulated viewing contrasts (negative > neutral), includes a clinical group (BPD) and healthy controls reported separately, and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates and cluster reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an empirical, task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs cognitive reappraisal/downregulation (Decrease vs Look) as the regulation strategy (I6). Emotional stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7). The paper reports separate results for bipolar patients and healthy controls (I8), includes within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. Negative Decrease > Negative Look) (I9), and performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and cluster correction reported in tables/figures (I10,I11). The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore it should be included.

This full text describes a task-based fMRI study instructing cognitive reappraisal of visual images in clinical participants and reports the within-task contrast ReappNeg > LookNeg; however, the analyses and results are presented using regional-of-interest (AAL-based ROI β weights) and PCA of those ROI values. The paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space in the main text or tables provided here. Therefore it meets the exclusion criterion for presenting ONLY ROI-based results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis (E4). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation—reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS images), I8 (sample includes clinical participants), I9 (reports a within-task contrast ReappNeg vs LookNeg). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps with peak coordinates reported). Full text appears complete for methods, results, and discussion.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and acceptance) while participants viewed visual sad images (IAPS and normed images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (accept > view, accept > reappraise, reappraise > view), includes both remitted MDD and control groups with results reported, and describes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses normalized to standard space with cluster coordinates reported in tables and figures. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual stimuli in BPD and HC and reports unregulated viewing contrasts, but participants were not instructed to use an emotion regulation strategy. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS/photographs), I8 (clinical sample with control group), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts such as negative > neutral). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation task — participants were explicitly instructed only to watch the pictures; the paradigm tested spontaneous/implicit pain-mediated affect regulation rather than an instructed strategy). I10 is ambiguous: whole-brain analyses were performed but yielded no FWE-significant clusters, and reported positive results rely on small-volume correction; however the decisive exclusion is failure to meet I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are directly violated. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not include an instructed emotion regulation task required by the review.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal (decrease negative) with visual stimuli (negative and neutral images). It includes adolescent clinical (CD) and typically developing control groups with within-task contrasts (decrease negative > look negative; look negative > look neutral) and reports group-level voxelwise SPM analyses normalized to standard space (MNI), including whole-brain and ROI-corrected results. Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an EEG/ERP study (dense-array EEG) of children performing an emotional go/no-go task; it is not an fMRI study and does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise fMRI activation maps. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (visual stimuli: facial images) and I8 (sample: children/clinical and control groups). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (task-based fMRI study absent), I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal/distancing/acceptance), I9 (no within-task fMRI emotion-regulation contrasts like reappraise>look; analyses are ERP amplitude comparisons rather than fMRI contrasts), and I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise fMRI results or peak coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper must be excluded from this fMRI emotion-regulation meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which participants (PTSD patients and matched healthy controls) were instructed to regulate emotional responses to visual stimuli (IAPS pictures) using explicit instructions to diminish (reappraisal), enhance, or maintain emotional responses. The paper reports within-task contrasts (negative-diminish, negative-enhance, negative-maintain) and between-group comparisons, and uses whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses with cluster correction. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a resting-state seed-based functional connectivity study predicting treatment response in bipolar disorder; it does not include any task-based emotion regulation paradigm. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without any whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample: clinical bipolar patients). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy/cognitive reappraisal), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli task), I9 (no within-task regulation contrasts reported), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked group-level maps), I11 (no task whole-brain results in text/tables). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (reappraise > negative view) and an unregulated viewing contrast (negative view > neutral view). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted with standard space coordinates and cluster/voxelwise corrections; results and peak coordinates are reported. The sample includes a clinical group (adult ADHD) and healthy controls with results reported separately. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (look/increase/decrease) of visually presented disgusting images (IAPS and in-house pictures) in ASD and TD youth. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (decrease-gross vs. look-gross; increase-gross vs. look-gross) and unregulated viewing contrasts, includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses normalized to Talairach space with results and tables/figures (supplemental tables referenced), and reports both ROI and PPI connectivity results. Sample includes clinical (ASD) and control groups with separate reporting. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (not truncated).

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli in clinical and control groups and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (I5, I7, I8, I9 met). However, the task is an implicit emotional conflict/matching task with no instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met). Analyses were conducted within a priori ROIs (PickAtlas) and activation reported from ROI-based voxelwise maps/extractions rather than a group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis with peak coordinates (I10 not met). This violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI/small-volume-corrected results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use a cognitive emotion regulation strategy (reappraisal/imagery) during presentation of visual conditioned stimuli (colored squares). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing Attend vs Regulate (e.g., Regulate CS+ vs Attend CS+), uses group-level whole-brain GLM analyses (thresholded maps, reported coordinates), and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Sample (healthy adult participants) is appropriate. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, includes task activation maps). Full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I11.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual IAPS pictures in BPD patients and healthy controls, with within-task contrasts (amygdala responses to unpleasant/neutral/pleasant pictures, and pre-post changes). However, the report focuses on an a priori amygdala ROI analysis and does not present any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (ROI-only results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Also, the fMRI task involved passive viewing with no instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met), though unregulated viewing contrasts are reported (I9 met). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I10. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of stress induction and an experimental incision with resting-state and seed-based connectivity analyses, not an instructed emotion-regulation task using visual emotional stimuli. The study does not instruct participants to use a regulation strategy (no reappraisal/distancing/etc.), does not use visual emotional stimuli as the target of regulation, and does not report within-task emotion-regulation contrasts or whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Primary analyses are resting-state amygdala activity/connectivity and regression over time. Therefore it fails the review's core inclusion requirements and meets exclusion E5 (only seed-based/resting-state analyses without a whole-brain task activation map).

This study is a resting-state fMRI analysis of negative affectivity/neuroticism in older adults and does not include any task-based emotion regulation paradigm or visual emotional stimuli. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity and ALFF analyses without any whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample: older adult participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy/cognitive reappraisal), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli/task; resting-state only), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present): fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore exclude from the meta-analysis of task-based emotion regulation fMRI studies.

This is a task-based fMRI study with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses and within-task contrasts (e.g., CS+E vs CS–) and an eligible sample, but it does not meet the core requirement that the fMRI task instructed participants to regulate their emotional response. The paradigm is fear conditioning/extinction and assesses recall of extinguished fear; participants underwent mindfulness training as an intervention between sessions but were not instructed to use a specific emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, acceptance) during the scanned task. Additionally, the paper does not explicitly state that the regulated stimuli were visual (stimulus modality not clearly described in the full text provided). Therefore I6 (instructed emotion-regulation task) is not met; I7 (explicitly visual stimuli) is also not confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply based on the provided text.

The article reports a task-based fMRI experiment that explicitly instructs emotion regulation via self-focused cognitive reappraisal (distancing/increasing), uses visual static stimuli (IAPS images), includes both a clinical (SAD) and control group with results reported separately, and presents within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (DistA > PermA, IncA > PermA) as well as an unregulated viewing contrast (PermA > PermN). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with thresholding and coordinate tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise Negative vs Look Negative) and also includes unregulated viewing contrasts (Look Negative vs Look Neutral; Emotional Faces vs Shapes). Stimuli are visual (IAPS images and emotional faces). Sample is treatment-seeking adults. Analyses include within-task contrasts and report whole-brain voxel-wise analyses with FDR correction; whole-brain activation details are noted as presented in Supplementary Materials. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and not an empathy task without regulation). Therefore the study meets I5–I11 and is eligible for inclusion.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that reports whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts of emotional script-driven imagery versus baseline (so it meets I5, I9, I10, I11 and I8). However it does NOT meet critical inclusion requirements: the task does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/distancing/acceptance instructions; participants were instructed to imagine the script), so I6 is not met. Also the emotional stimuli are auditory script-driven imagery rather than visual stimuli (no images or video), so I7 is not met. Therefore the study is excluded.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study using visual IAPS stimuli and reports within-task contrasts (EXP neg > neut; PRES neg > neut) and coordinates, but it did not instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy during the task. Participants were grouped by habitual self-report (ERQ) rather than given instructions to reappraise, suppress, or otherwise regulate during scanning. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (task includes an instructed emotion-regulation strategy) is not met, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered by the paper. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of regret in a decision-making paradigm (sequential ‘devil’ task) with visual feedback and group whole-brain analyses, but participants were not instructed to use any emotion-regulation strategy. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli/feedback), I8 (eligible samples including healthy and clinical groups), I9 (within-task contrasts related to emotional responses to missed opportunities), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I11 (results described and supported by supplementary materials). Inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as cognitive reappraisal or other instructed regulation) is not met because the study assessed natural/regulatory responses to outcomes without instructing participants to regulate their emotions (no reappraise/look or down-/up-regulate instructions). Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This study is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI investigation using visual stimuli (happy faces) in a healthy sample and reports group-level peak coordinates, but it does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy as defined by the review. Instead, participants performed a mood induction / instructed generation of positive mood (“try to become happy” using faces and autobiographical memories). The meta-analysis requires an explicit instructed emotion regulation strategy (e.g., cognitive reappraisal, acceptance, instructed cognitive control) during stimulus viewing (I6), which is not present here. The paper does report within-task (happy > baseline) analyses and whole-brain maps (meeting I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11), but fails to meet I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore EXCLUDED.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed cognitive reappraisal (meets I5 and I6). It reports within-task contrasts (reappraise vs react) and whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with coordinates/tables (meets I9, I10, I11). Sample includes patients and healthy controls with separate reporting (meets I8). However, the emotional stimuli were participant-generated autobiographical scripts presented as sentences and flashed negative self-belief words (text). The review's inclusion criterion I7 excludes studies whose regulated stimuli are word- or sentence-based (non-visual stimuli). Therefore this study fails I7 and must be excluded. Exclusion criteria: none met.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed participants to down-regulate emotional responses via amygdala neurofeedback (I6) while viewing visual aversive pictures (I7). Sample (N=32 healthy adults) meets I8, and the paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g. ‘regulate > view’; I9). However, the article reports only seed-based/effective connectivity analyses (PPI, DCM) and does not present a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map (conventional activation contrast results) in the manuscript (these activation results are deferred to a prior publication). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (connectivity-only without accompanying whole-brain task activation map) and fails I10. Full text appears complete. Exclusion applied due to E5.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (static pictures, IAPS and spider photographs). The paper reports within-task contrasts (up > look, down > look; look negative > neutral; spider > aversive) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates and cluster thresholds, alongside ROI analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; includes whole-brain analyses; contains within-group task effects; not a perspective-taking-only empathy study). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5–I11) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (‘Reduce’) versus ‘Maintain’ (I5, I6). Stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7). Sample includes adolescents with MDD and matched healthy controls with results reported for groups (I8). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts (Maintain vs Reduce, Reduce vs Maintain) (I9). The paper describes and reports a whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis with cluster-thresholding and ROI analysis; whole-brain group effects are described (I10) and results/figures/tables are reported in the text (I11). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, includes whole-brain activation maps and within-task effects, not only connectivity or ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a PET task study of working memory, not an fMRI emotion-regulation study. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (visual stimuli: letter/spatial displays), I8 (eligible adult sample), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses reported), I11 (results reported with coordinates/figures). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (task-based fMRI study — this is PET, not fMRI), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy; tasks were working-memory, not reappraisal/acceptance/distancing), I9 (no emotion-regulation or unregulated emotional viewing contrasts; contrasts are working-memory load vs. control). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) specifically apply, but failure to meet core inclusion criteria (notably I5, I6, I9) mandates exclusion. fulltext appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (violent vs non-violent video game events) and reports within-task contrasts comparing violent and non-violent events (unregulated viewing contrasts). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (maps, thresholding, peak coordinates and tables). Sample is healthy adults (male), satisfying participant inclusion. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given, the review’s inclusion rules accept unregulated viewing contrasts (per I9), so the study qualifies. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports within-task effects). Full text is complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study instructing cognitive reappraisal of negative visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task regulation and viewing contrasts (Reappraise Negative > Attend Negative; View Negative > View Neutral), presents group- and within-group whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables/coordinates and FWE-corrected results, and includes complete methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs Attend/Negative), using visual IAPS images as stimuli. It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraise > Negative; Negative > Reappraise), presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and FDR-corrected results, and includes full methods, results, and discussion for an eligible sample (undergraduate high/low psychosis-proneness). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is empirical, reports whole-brain results (not ROI-only), includes within-task effects (not only between-group interactions), and is not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation instructions. Full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (reality checking) while presenting visual emotional stimuli (negative faces) in healthy adults and reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. "view > regulate") and coordinates for amygdala effects, the paper’s results are reported using ROI-based analyses and individual/ROI peaks rather than a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. The review requires at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis with peak coordinates in standard space (I10). Because the study presents only ROI-constrained findings and no accompanying whole-brain group map, it meets exclusion criterion E4. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (regulate vs. maintain) of visual stimuli (negative and neutral pictures) in a clinical sample (BPD) with healthy controls. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > view, regulate > maintain) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected results, plus ROI and connectivity analyses. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply: this is empirical original fMRI data with whole-brain task activation maps (not solely ROI, connectivity-only, or non-task paradigms), and the task is explicit emotion regulation rather than perspective-taking without regulation instruction. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain group analyses; however it does NOT instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing) — participants were instructed to identify facial expressions while ignoring superimposed words (an emotional conflict Stroop). Therefore it does not meet the critical inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample includes clinical and control groups reported), I9 (reports within-task contrasts related to emotional conflict/monitoring vs resolution), and I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy). No exclusion criteria from the provided list (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This full-text reports an original, task-based fMRI experiment that directly matches the review objective. Inclusion criteria met: (I5) task-based fMRI; (I6) instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal: downregulate and upregulate); (I7) visual stimuli (IAPS pictures); (I8) sample qualifies (healthy adult groups reported separately); (I9) reports within-task contrasts (downregulate vs negative look, upregulate vs negative look, negative look vs neutral); (I10) whole-brain, group-level voxelwise RFX ANOVA with corrected thresholds; (I11) results presented as tables/figures with peak coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group task effects). The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.
