This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal during presentation of visual IAPS images and reports the within-task contrast reappraise > view. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are performed and peak coordinates (MNI) are reported (e.g., 56 20 8), satisfying whole-brain evidence. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed cognitive reappraisal (an emotion-regulation strategy) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images). The sample (adolescent girls with PTSD) is an eligible participant group. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraise negative v. view negative; view negative v. view neutral) and conducts whole-brain, voxel-wise analyses producing significant clusters (Table 2) with standard-space localization and cluster-thresholding; task activation data are also referenced in supplementary figures. Although the primary imaging analyses emphasize task-modulated functional connectivity, these are whole-brain, voxelwise task-contrast maps tied to the instructed regulation task, satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., the study is empirical, not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, and includes within-group task effects). Full text is complete.

This RCT is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (meta-cognitive attention/‘observe’ condition) (I6), includes a clinical SAD sample (I8), reports within-task regulation contrasts (regulate vs react NSBs) (I9) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (I10, I11). However, the emotional stimuli consist of participant-generated autobiographical narratives and negative self-beliefs presented as written sentences/words (scripted sentences and flashed NSBs). The review’s inclusion criterion I7 explicitly excludes studies whose regulated stimuli are word and sentence stimuli. Because the regulated stimuli are non-qualifying (words/sentences), the study does not meet I7 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed cognitive reappraisal (Reduce vs. Maintain) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (Reduce > Maintain and group contrasts), presents whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and tables/figures of significant clusters, and reports results separately for high-anxiety and control groups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete for screening purposes.

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli in an eligible sample and reports whole-brain results with peak coordinates, it does NOT meet the core emotion-regulation inclusion requirement. The fMRI task probes emotional conflict (incongruent vs. congruent trials) and measures behavioral/neural responses, but participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance) nor is there a within-task regulation contrast (e.g., reappraise > look). Also no simple unregulated viewing contrast (e.g., emotion > baseline or negative > neutral) is reported as the qualifying contrast for this review. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (required) and I9. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I9. Exclusion criteria met: none (no applicable exclusion criteria were triggered).

Meets all review inclusion criteria: This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) with detailed methods and results. Stimuli were visual IAPS images (aversive and neutral). The sample (college-aged participants; clinical/high EXT and low EXT groups reported separately) qualifies. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g., aversive-reappraise > aversive-maintain; AR > AM) and unregulated viewing contrasts (AM > NM). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with MNI normalization and cluster thresholds; results are presented in text/figures and coordinates. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext is complete.

This is a resting-state, seed-based connectivity fMRI study in adolescent marijuana users; no task was administered and no emotion-regulation instructions or visual emotional stimuli were used. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample of adolescents qualifies). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli; resting-state), I9 (no within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked group-level activation maps). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs Maintain) using visual IAPS images, included both unmedicated panic disorder patients and healthy controls with separate group analyses, and reported within-task contrasts (Reappraise vs Maintain, Maintain vs Reappraise) and other task effects. The paper provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding and MNI coordinates, and reports results in the text/ROIs and connectivity analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

Although this paper is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps, it does not instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, or other instructed regulation). The task contrasts are emotional-valence judgments versus geometric judgments (emotion > geometry), not explicit regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look) — so inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not met. Satisfied inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample includes patients and controls reported separately), I9 (reports within-task contrasts related to emotional viewing), I10 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps with FWE correction), I11 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I6 (instructed emotion regulation). Full text appears complete (not incomplete).

Full text contains a complete task-based fMRI study in which participants (N=60 women with BPD) performed an emotion regulation task using instructed cognitive reappraisal/distancing (‘distance’ vs ‘immerse’) while viewing visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts assessing both unregulated viewing (immerse/aversive > immerse/neutral) and regulation (distance/aversive > immerse/aversive), and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with peak MNI coordinates and correction details (FWE and SVC). The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. Thus it satisfies the review’s inclusion criteria for task fMRI with instructed visual emotion regulation and whole-brain reporting.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of visual emotion processing (meets I5, I7, I8, I9) but does NOT meet key inclusion requirements: no instructed emotion-regulation strategy was used (I6 not met), and the reported analyses are ROI-only without any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) activation maps or peak coordinates (I10 not met). Because it reports ONLY ROI results with no whole-brain analysis, it violates exclusion criterion E4. Therefore it must be excluded.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation using visual IAPS stimuli and reports within-task contrasts with peak coordinates, but the methods and results indicate that targeted ROI analyses (anatomically defined ROIs using the WFU PickAtlas) were used and thresholds are described for ROI analyses. The paper does not clearly report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation analysis or whole-brain results outside ROI masks in the main text (whole-brain results are not presented; within-group whole-brain maps are referenced as Supplementary Material but not shown here). Therefore it appears to report only ROI-constrained voxelwise results and peak coordinates, which meets exclusion criterion E4. Detailed: (a) Exclusion met: E4; (b) Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation - reappraisal and distraction), I7 (visual stimuli - IAPS pictures), I8 (sample qualifies; controls reported separately), I9 (reports within-task contrasts such as reappraise>view, view negative>neutral), I11 (coordinates reported in text/figures); (c) Inclusion NOT met: I10 (no clear whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation map reported). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (decrease vs look) using visual IAPS photographs in patients with MDD and matched controls. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., negative decrease > negative look) and random-effects whole-brain voxelwise group analyses with cluster-thresholded maps and coordinates, and results are described in the text and figures. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) that explicitly instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal during a reappraisal block versus an attend block (I6). The regulated stimuli are visual (adolescent face photos and on-screen feedback) (I7). The sample (adolescents, clinical and control groups) is acceptable (I8). The analysis reports a within-task contrast of interest (reappraisal > attend) (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are reported with peak coordinates in standard space (e.g., right frontal pole x=20,y=64,z=18) (I10), and results/coordinates are clearly described in the text (I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper includes whole-brain activation maps (not ROI-only), reports task activation contrasts (not only connectivity), and is empirical. Full article content (background, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study with whole-brain analyses (Talairach space) and an eligible sample, it does NOT meet the meta-analysis’ core requirement that an emotion-regulation strategy be instructed and tested with emotional visual stimuli. Specifically: inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample acceptable), I10 (whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps), I11 (results reported in text/figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation; participants were not told to reappraise or otherwise regulate emotion), I7 (stimuli are math/problems and words—not visual emotional stimuli such as IAPS images, faces, or films), I9 (no within-task contrast testing instructed emotion regulation vs. view; contrasts are math>word or cue effects, not reappraise>look or similar). No exclusion criteria from the review list (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) with an appropriate sample (soldiers and civilians; I8) and reports within-task contrasts (unfair > fair) relevant to emotional responding (I9). The paper also provides group-level ROI coordinates in standard (Talairach) space (I10) and reports these results in the text (I11). However, the study does NOT instruct participants to use any emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other instructed regulation); participants responded naturally to an anger-provoking interactive Ultimatum Game, so inclusion criterion I6 is not met. In addition, the emotional stimulus is an interpersonal, largely verbal/interactive provocation (live negotiations) rather than a visual stimulus set (I7 not met). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I6 (and I7) are not met, the study is excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered by this paper.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly investigates an instructed cognitive emotion regulation strategy (distraction) using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The sample includes PTSD patients and trauma-exposed controls with results reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (distract-negative > attend-negative) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and whole-brain FWE-corrected results. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is empirical, not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, and includes within-group task effects). Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Full text reports a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed emotion regulation strategies (reappraise and distract) during presentation of visual sad images, with within-task contrasts (e.g., Sad-Reappraise > Sad-View, Sad-Distract > Sad-View). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported with peak coordinates in MNI space. Sample and full methods/results/discussion are present in the article. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; includes whole-brain task activation maps; not limited to connectivity-only; contains within-task effects; not an empathy/perspective-taking only study).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (diminish/enhance/maintain) using cognitive reappraisal-like strategies, with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It reports within-task contrasts (diminish>maintain, enhance>maintain), and performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and thresholds described. Participant groups (PTSD, trauma-exposed non-PTSD, healthy controls) are reported separately. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the emotional stimuli used are experimenter-selected negative self-belief sentences (word/sentence stimuli presented as text), which do not meet the review's visual-stimulus requirement. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation task—breath-focused attention and distraction), I8 (eligible sample; clinical population reported), I9 (within-task contrasts reported: breath-focused > react, distraction > react, react > baseline), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates), I11 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I7 (stimuli are word/sentence textual probes, which the protocol specifies should be excluded). No exclusion criteria from E3–E7 apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to regulate emotion (increase/decrease) using cognitive reappraisal/distancing, using visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (increase>maintain, decrease>maintain) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level correction and reported peak voxels in standard space. Clinical and control groups are reported separately. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I5–I11) and violates no exclusion criteria. Sample size is modest but acceptable; full text appears complete.

This is a task-based, task-evoked fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images). Participants are combat-exposed veterans with and without PTSD reported separately. The main contrast Reappraise > Maintain (and Maintain > Look) is reported, and whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and tables are provided (with SVC only for the a priori amygdala ROI). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports within-task effects, and not an empathy/perspective-taking task). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11 and should be INCLUDED.

The full text is complete. This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (I5, I7), includes an eligible sample and separate control group reporting (I8), reports within-task emotional contrasts and unregulated viewing effects (aversive > target and aversive condition maps) (I9), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates (I10, I11). However, the study does NOT instruct any emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing or similar); aversive images were task-irrelevant distractors in an oddball detection task rather than a regulated condition, so I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Because all inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I6 is not met, the study must be excluded.

Full-text screening decision: EXCLUDED because the regulated stimuli are not visual images but personalized, script-driven worry and reappraisal sentences (word/sentence stimuli). This fails inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be VISUAL; exclude script-driven imagery or word/sentence stimuli). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI/ASL task), I6 (instructed emotion regulation — cognitive reappraisal blocks were trained and instructed), I8 (sample acceptable — older adults, clinical and control groups), I9 (reports within-task contrasts: worry induction vs rest, reappraisal vs rest, block effects, regressions), I10 (performed group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task analyses in SPM12), I11 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (visual stimuli). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded on the basis of non-visual, script-driven stimuli.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed an emotion regulation strategy (distancing/reappraisal) while participants viewed visual emotional images (IAPS/Emopics). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., positive watch > positive distance; positive watch > neutral) and conducted whole-brain group-level analyses (results reported, with whole-brain correction; supplementary tables/figures referenced). Sample includes both anorexia nervosa patients and healthy controls with group-level results reported. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary materials are referenced but not required to confirm whole-brain reporting. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion: The study uses task-based fMRI neurofeedback with instructed emotion up-regulation (happy autobiographical recall) in healthy participants and reports within-task contrasts (Happy Memories vs Rest) and ROI-based analyses; thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation/self-regulation), I8 (sample), and I9 (within-task contrast). However, the regulated emotional stimuli are internally generated autobiographical memories rather than external VISUAL emotional stimuli (violates I7). Critically, the paper reports ROI and effective-connectivity (SVAR/VAR) results and GLM ROI percent-signal analyses but does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-activation map with peak coordinates in standard space; analyses are not whole-brain task activations but ROI/connectivity-focused. Therefore it violates inclusion I10 and falls under exclusion criteria E4 and E5 (only ROI/effective-connectivity results with no whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete for screening.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (an emotion regulation strategy) using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures) in adolescents (patients and healthy controls). The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > Maintain, Maintain > Reappraise, and emotion > baseline) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with standard space results (cluster thresholding reported). All relevant inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion criteria met: E5 — this paper reports only resting-state analyses and correlations with behavioral change; it does not present any whole-brain task-evoked activation maps or task-based contrast images. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (an emotion-regulation task was instructed), I7 (visual stimuli—fearful pictures), I8 (sample qualifies). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the manuscript does not report task-based fMRI results for the current analyses), I9 (no within-task contrasts related to regulation are reported here), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or peak coordinates are provided). The full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis because it reports only resting-state analyses without accompanying whole-brain task activation maps (E5) despite having the required task/stimuli and sample characteristics.

Excluded because the study does not test an instructed emotion-regulation task and reports only ROI/small-volume-corrected analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample includes patients and healthy controls), I9 (reports a within-task contrast: sch-evaluation > cc-evaluation). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instruction to regulate emotion — participants rated statements rather than being instructed to reappraise or otherwise regulate), I7 (stimuli are word/sentence statements rather than visual images/films; the review excludes studies with word/sentence stimuli), I10 (no clear whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-activation map reported—main findings are small-volume/ROI-corrected). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (results are reported with small-volume/ROI correction and no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Full text appears complete for screening.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) and an instructed manipulation (‘maintain’ vs ‘non-maintain’) that constitutes an instructed strategy to control/maintain emotional response. The paper reports within-task contrasts (maintain > non-maintain for negative and positive emotions) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard (Talairach) space. The sample and analyses meet the review’s inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, include within-task effects, and this is not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli (I5, I7), an eligible participant sample (I8), within-task unregulated viewing contrasts reported (Disgust>Neutral, Fear>Neutral) (I9), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported (I10, I11). However, the fMRI task did not instruct any emotion regulation strategy—participants passively viewed pictures and no reappraise/ regulate instruction or regulation contrast is present—so inclusion criterion I6 (instruction of an emotion regulation strategy) is not met. Therefore the study does not meet ALL required inclusion criteria and is excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) and reports a within-task unregulated viewing contrast (negative > positive) with whole-brain analyses. The manuscript includes methods, results, and discussion and reports group-level whole-brain activations (with supplementary whole-brain images) and ROI follow-ups. Although no instructed emotion-regulation strategy was used, the review accepts unregulated viewing contrasts; thus the study meets the review’s objective. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrast relevant to emotion), I10 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analysis), I11 (results reported/described with figures/supplementary materials). No exclusion criteria were met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (“realize being safe”) during picture presentation and reports within-task regulation contrasts (negative-safe vs negative-look) and unregulated viewing contrasts (negative-look vs neutral-look). Stimuli are visual social pictures (IAPS and additional erotic images). Sample includes patients (BPD, cluster-C) and nonpatient controls with group-level analyses reported separately. The manuscript reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with thresholded F maps and cluster coordinates in Talairach space (tables/figures). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using visual IAPS images and reports within-task contrasts and peak coordinates/whole-brain displays, it does NOT instruct participants to use an explicit emotion regulation strategy. The task requires cognitive control with irrelevant affective distractors (MSIT-IAPS) but participants were not told to reappraise, accept, distance, or otherwise regulate their emotional responses. Therefore Inclusion Criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not met, so the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on instructed emotion regulation.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and distraction) while participants viewed visual emotional images (IAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraisal vs view; distraction vs view) and unregulated viewing contrasts. Analyses were conducted as group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses in SPM8 with normalization to standard space and report thresholding at FWE-corrected levels; the methods state that whole-brain FWE-corrected results are reported. Samples include clinical (BD patients), unaffected relatives, and matched controls with group-level results reported separately. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study presenting visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) during an emotional-attention paradigm and reports within-task contrasts comparing negative/positive to neutral (e.g., attending negative > neutral; ignoring negative > neutral). It includes whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space and reports results for participant groups separately. Although no explicit instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I6) was used, the meta-analysis objective permits inclusion of studies that report unregulated viewing/attending contrasts; the paper provides such contrasts (satisfying I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 and is appropriate for inclusion.

Exclusion E4 met: the study reports only ROI-based analyses (AAL mask extractions of rACC, dACC, amygdala) and explicitly states no conclusions can be made at the whole-brain level. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (explicit instructed emotion regulation task - Reappraise vs Maintain), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS images and face photographs), I8 (clinical patient sample acceptable), I9 (within-task contrasts reported, e.g., Reappraise > Maintain; Look > fixation; Threat Low > High). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or reported peak coordinates in standard space). Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to provide whole-brain task-evoked results and reporting only ROI results.

This study is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI experiment that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (thought suppression/self-distraction) and reports within-task contrasts and peak coordinates; however, the regulated stimuli are not visual: anxiety was induced via anticipation of painful electrical stimulation and auditory cues, and no visual emotional stimuli were presented. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain maps with coordinates), I11 (results described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs participants to use cognitive-linguistic regulation (reappraisal-style) versus a 'look' condition, with within-task contrasts reported (Regulate > Look and Look emotion > Neutral). Emotional stimuli are visual static photographs (harsh faces and violent scenes). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates in Talairach space and tables/figures of activations. Both patient (SAD) and healthy control groups are analyzed and reported separately. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete and satisfies all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (explicit "reality checking" cognitive control) during the anticipation period, matching the meta-analysis scope. Stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (static images). The sample is healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts (expectation negative vs neutral, unknown vs neutral) for the cognitive-control group and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with Talairach coordinates and tables/figures. Results relevant to regulation (cognitive-control vs basic/no-control) are reported. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review only, ROI-only results, only between-group effects without within-group task effects, non-visual stimuli, or pure perspective-taking) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs cognitive reappraisal (LOOK/DECREASE) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS). The sample includes a clinical group (IGD) and matched controls with results reported for groups separately. The paper reports within-task effects (condition main effects and condition contrasts such as Neutral/Look/Decrease, ROI comparisons) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with standard-space peak coordinates and corrected thresholds (voxel p<0.001, pFWE<0.05). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study with whole-brain results and coordinate reporting, but it does not meet the review's core requirement that participants were instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (eligible sample), I10 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), I11 (results reported with peak coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instruction to regulate emotion — task was an executive Go/No-Go with feedback, not reappraisal or other instructed regulation), I7 (regulated stimuli are not emotional visual stimuli such as IAPS photographs or films — stimuli were letters and brief visual negative feedback words), I9 (no within-task contrast corresponding to emotion regulation or unregulated emotional viewing; contrasts are EC>CH and VNF>CH but not framed as emotion regulation or unregulated emotional stimulus viewing). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) appear to apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: the emotion regulation strategy was not instructed. The manipulation used incidental/implicit reappraisal via preceding descriptions and participants passively viewed images without being instructed to regulate their emotional responses. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS images), I8 (sample: healthy adult participants), I9 (reports within-task contrast related to regulation: NNEG-DESC > NEG-DESC), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates reported), I11 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (regulation instructed). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a resting-state functional connectivity study with participants instructed to lie passively; there is no task, no instructed emotion regulation, and no visual emotional stimuli. Therefore it does not meet the task-based and task-contrast requirements. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only resting-state analyses without any whole-brain task activation map) and E6 (no within-task task effect or within-task contrasts reported). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample criteria: human participants; clinical groups characterized). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or viewing contrasts), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps; I11 consequently not applicable). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of PTSD that instructs cognitive reappraisal (‘‘decrease’’ vs ‘‘look’’) using visual IAPS pictures. It reports within-task regulation contrasts (reappraise/decrease > look) and task-evoked voxel-wise group-level analyses (voxel-wise linear mixed-effects models with voxel-wise FDR correction) with results and peak coordinates referenced in supplemental tables/figures. Participants are a clinical PTSD sample (randomized treatment vs waiting list) and results include whole-brain/voxel-wise analyses (including exploratory whole-brain analyses and masked voxel-wise maps) and reported task activation findings. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion IDs met: E5 (study reports only resting-state analyses/ALFF pre/post-task without any whole-brain task-evoked activation map of an emotion-regulation task). Inclusion IDs met: I8 (sample criteria satisfied — older adults including MCI and controls). Inclusion IDs NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation; fMRI was resting-state pre/post-task), I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; cognitive tasks were not emotion-regulation instructions), I7 (regulated stimuli are not visual emotional stimuli — tasks were cognitive challenges outside scanner), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation contrasts such as reappraise>view or emotion>baseline), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore exclude.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using an instructed emotion-labeling condition (label > observe) as the regulation manipulation (I6), with visual face stimuli (I7), an adolescent sample (I8), and a within-task regulation contrast reported (I9). However, the paper reports seed-based PPI connectivity results focused on an a priori rVLPFC ROI (and amygdala seed) and does not present any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I10 and meets exclusion criteria E4 (ROI-only results/no whole-brain analysis) and E5 (only seed-based connectivity reported without whole-brain task activation). Full text appears complete. Accordingly, I exclude this study.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (faces) and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (negative > neutral), but it does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy. Critically, all reported neuroimaging results are ROI-based directional connectivity and VBM analyses; the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation map (only a priori ROI analyses and connectivity), so it violates exclusion criteria for ROI-only/partial-coverage reports. Therefore excluded (E4, E5). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrast). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise map), I11 (not applicable because no whole-brain results presented). Full text appears complete.

This is a resting-state fMRI study using stochastic DCM to estimate directed/effective connectivity in PTSD, PTSD+DS, and controls. It does not involve any task or instructed emotion-regulation paradigm, nor any visual emotional stimuli or within-task regulation contrasts. Therefore it fails the task-based and stimulus-related inclusion criteria required for the meta-analysis. Exclusion criteria E5 applies (study reports only resting-state/effective-connectivity analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). The study meets inclusion criterion I8 (sample type is acceptable — clinical and control groups reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation task), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I9 (within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map), and I11 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain task results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study (SEAT) using visual stimuli (composite faces and scenes) and an instructed emotion-regulation manipulation via attention shifting (Indoor/Outdoor vs Male/Female), satisfying the review’s definition of an instructed antecedent-focused regulation strategy. The paper reports within-task contrasts including Indoor/Outdoor—Male/Female and Male/Female—Face/Place, and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise analyses with reported peak coordinates and cluster localization (Brodmann/AAL3). Both PTSD and healthy control groups are included and compared, with within-group effects also tested. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-only paradigms) are met. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11) are fulfilled and the study should be INCLUDED.

Exclusion: E7 applies — participants were instructed to take the protagonist’s perspective (perspective-taking) with no instruction to amplify or dampen emotion, so this is an empathy/perspective-taking design rather than an emotion regulation instruction. Inclusion: I5 (task-based fMRI) is met; I8 (sample: clinical patients with controls reported separately) is met; I9 (reports an unregulated emotion contrast: anger > neutral) is met. Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy — reappraisal/acceptance/distancing not instructed), I7 (emotional stimuli are auditory stories, not VISUAL stimuli), I10 (no clearly reported whole-brain, group-level task activation peaks reported for the key emotion contrasts — reported results rely on ROI/SVC findings). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not use visual emotional stimuli and does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy, and it primarily reports ROI/SVC results for the key contrasts (E7 explicitly met).

The full text describes a task-based fMRI study implementing an instructed cognitive reappraisal paradigm (Reduce vs Maintain) using visual negative images in adolescents with MDD and matched healthy controls. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Pre-Reduce vs Pre-Maintain) addressing reappraisal success, and conducts voxelwise whole-brain group-level analyses (ANCOVA) with results in standard MNI space; amygdala ROI analyses are also described. The manuscript includes full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study used resting-state (eyes-closed) fMRI and multivariate/functional connectivity analyses to classify PTSD subtypes; there is no task paradigm, no instruction to regulate emotion, and no visual emotional stimuli or within-task regulation contrasts reported. It therefore does not provide task-evoked, within-task emotion regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts nor whole-brain task activation maps. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses without a task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample qualifies: clinical and control groups). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I9 (within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), I10 (whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I11 (N/A reporting of task results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not perform a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation experiment. Although it uses visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) and an eligible sample (elderly adults), the fMRI data are resting-state and effective/seed-based connectivity analyses; the Emotion Processing Task (EPT) was behavioral and performed outside the scanner. Therefore it lacks any task-evoked, within-task fMRI contrasts or whole-brain task activation maps required for inclusion. Exclusion ID met: E5 (reports only resting-state/seed/effective connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion IDs met: I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I6 (instructed emotion regulation task), I9 (within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing fMRI contrast), I10 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports within-task contrasts (emotion/faces > shapes) and whole-brain group-level analyses with peak coordinates. Although the task did not instruct emotion regulation (so I6 not met), the meta-analysis objective accepts unregulated viewing contrasts (I9), and the study meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (clinical sample acceptable), I9 (unregulated viewing contrast reported), I10 (whole-brain group analyses with coordinates), and I11 (results reported in text/supplement). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (ACCEPT vs REACT) and applies it to visual emotional stimuli (IAPS negative vs neutral images). It reports within-task contrasts (ACCEPT > REACT; Negative > Neutral) for images, includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with corrected results and coordinates, and provides sufficient methodological detail and results (introduction, methods, results, discussion). The sample is healthy adults. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study is task-based (I5) and uses visual stimuli (movie clips) (I7). The sample (healthy young adult women) is acceptable (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts of unregulated viewing (proposal unfair > proposal fair) and decision contrasts (I9), and reports whole-brain, group-level analyses with thresholding and tables/figures (I10,I11). However, the study did not instruct participants to use any emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/acceptance instructions); participants played the Ultimatum Game and made natural decisions—so inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation task) is not met. No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I6). Included criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11. Included criteria not met: I6. Exclusion criteria applied: none ( []). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation (I5) with an eligible sample (I8) and reports whole-brain task activation results/coordinates (I10, I11). However, it does NOT investigate instructed emotion regulation: the task is a Parametric Go/No-Go using non-emotional letter stimuli and there is no instruction to regulate emotional responses, so it fails I6 (no emotion-regulation strategy instructed) and I7 (stimuli are not emotional visual stimuli). It also does not report any within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (e.g., reappraise>look), so it fails I9. None of the exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the paper does not meet the core emotion-regulation-in-fMRI inclusion requirements for this meta-analysis and should be excluded.

This full text reports an empirical task-based fMRI study in which participants were explicitly instructed to regulate emotion (reduce negative, enhance positive) using CBT-like cognitive reappraisal/’reality checking’ strategies while viewing visual emotional scenes (IAPS). The paper presents within-task contrasts (reduce vs attend, enhance vs attend), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and FWE correction, and separate patient (MDD) and control group results. The manuscript includes complete methods, results, and discussion, and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to apply causal attributions (an instructed reappraisal strategy) while viewing visual stimuli (static face photographs). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (internal>view, external>view, emotion-specific contrasts) at the group level and presents whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level multiple-comparisons correction and reported coordinates/tables. Participant groups include MDD and matched healthy controls with results reported by group. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (task, imaging, preprocessing, statistics), Results (behavioral, fMRI, connectivity) and Discussion, so the full article appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no resting-state-only, no purely perspective-taking without emotion regulation). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11) and the study should be INCLUDED.

Excluded because the emotional stimuli used are internally-evoked autobiographical memories rather than external VISUAL stimuli, so the study fails inclusion criterion I7. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation/cognitive control via neurofeedback), I8 (sample: clinical MDD group), I9 (reports within-task contrasts, e.g., Happy vs Rest and neurofeedback-related contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses/PPI maps), I11 (whole-brain results clearly described). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED based on not meeting I7 (visual stimuli).

This full-text is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the SEAT paradigm (visual composite images of faces/scenes) and reports group-level task activation results with MNI coordinates. The task includes instructed emotion modulation conditions (attentional modulation and an appraisal ‘Like/Dislike’ condition constituting instructed cognitive appraisal/regulation). Analyses include within-task contrasts/condition effects (implicit emotion processing vs baseline; condition effects) and whole-brain random-effects maps with voxelwise and SVC results reported. Sample (healthy adult males) is eligible. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly addresses instructed emotion regulation. Inclusion criteria met: (I5) task-based fMRI; (I6) an instructed regulation strategy (detach/distancing) was used; (I7) visual stimuli (IAPS/EmoPicS images) were presented; (I8) healthy adult sample reported; (I9) within-task contrasts are reported (permit negative > permit neutral; detach negative > permit negative, etc.); (I10/I11) the authors report exploratory whole-brain analyses and refer to tables/figures/supplementary materials for whole-brain results. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and References; no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual emotional stimuli (fearful and neutral faces) with a clear within-task unregulated viewing contrast (fearful > neutral). Group-level whole-brain analyses are reported with peak coordinates in standard space. The sample includes a clinical PTSD group and traumatized controls reported separately. Although no emotion-regulation instruction was given, the meta-analysis objective explicitly accepts unregulated viewing contrasts, and this study provides the required task-evoked, whole-brain data. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the required emotion-regulation instruction criterion. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I7 (visual stimuli—faces), I8 (sample includes clinical and control groups), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts, e.g., happy>fixation, fearful>fixation), I10 (reports group-level whole-brain analyses), I11 (results reported with coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; task is gender-labeling/implicit processing rather than instructed reappraisal or other regulation). Exclusion criteria applied: none ([]) . Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded because I6 is not satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to ignore emotional face distracters (an instructed cognitive control of emotional responses), using visual stimuli (emotional faces). It reports within-task contrasts comparing conditions with emotional distracters versus no-distracters (e.g., 2-back + fear > 2-back + no-distracters) and presents group-level task-evoked activation results (working memory network whole-brain effects) as well as ROI analyses and PPI connectivity; patient and control groups are reported separately. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting, non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for task fMRI emotion regulation with visual stimuli.

This study is a resting-state fMRI investigation of cortical–amygdala connectivity during anticipation of public speaking in social anxiety disorder, not a task-based emotion-regulation fMRI study with instructed regulation of visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample includes clinical and control groups reported separately). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; participants were not instructed to regulate), I7 (regulated stimuli are not visual; the manipulation is verbal/social threat, not visual emotional stimuli), I9 (no within-task regulation contrasts such as ‘reappraise > look’), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for an emotion-regulation task). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only resting-state/connectivity analyses without a whole-brain task activation map) and E6 (primarily reports group interactions in connectivity with no within-task regulation effect/contrast). Therefore the study does not satisfy the meta-analysis requirements and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy closely mapping onto cognitive reappraisal (“analyze” vs “feel”) (I6). It reports within-task regulation contrasts (feel > analyze) (I9), and presents whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses with coordinates (I10,I11). The sample (MDD patients and healthy controls) is eligible (I8). However, the regulated stimuli are negative autobiographical memories recalled via cue phrases (script-driven imagery/internal recall), not externally presented visual stimuli (images or video). Therefore it fails stimulus eligibility (I7), which is required for inclusion in this meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because I7 (visual-stimulus requirement) is not met; included criteria satisfied: I5, I6, I8, I9, I10, I11; excluded criteria met: none.

This is a resting-state fMRI study comparing bipolar mania, euthymia, and healthy controls; no task was administered and no emotion-regulation instructions or task contrasts are reported. Exclusion applied: E5 (study reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without any task activation maps). Inclusion met: I8 (sample includes participant groups). Inclusions not met: I5 (not task-based), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation/cognitive reappraisal), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli used), I9 (no within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked group-level activation maps). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded from the meta-analysis focused on task-based emotion-regulation fMRI.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (individually tailored pictures) with instructed task conditions including an appraisal condition and an explicit distraction task (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy). The paper reports within-task contrasts (appraisal vs implicit baseline; conditionwise PPI contrasts such as OCD-relevant v. aversive and distraction v. appraisal) and presents group-level whole-brain GLM results (Fig.1 and Supplementary Table S2) with peak coordinates in standard space. Participants include unmedicated OCD patients and matched healthy controls with results reported separately. Thus the study meets criteria for task-based fMRI, instructed regulation (distraction), visual stimuli, sample, relevant within-task contrasts, and whole-brain reporting. Full text appears complete.

Full text is not available (API error message: 'API rate limit exceeded'); core article content (methods, results) cannot be assessed. Therefore I cannot verify any required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria not met (unable to confirm): I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample reporting), I9 (within-task or viewing contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates), I11 (clear reporting of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria can be confirmed from the available metadata. Because the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending full-text access.

This article meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal; decrease vs attend) (I6). The regulated stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7). Participant groups include depressed patients and matched controls (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (negative decrease > negative attend) (I9). Analyses are voxel-wise, mixed-effects, whole-brain group-level maps with cluster correction and reported clusters/coordinates (Table 1 / text) satisfying whole-brain evidence (I10) and reporting results in text/tables (I11). Full text contains intro, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (individually tailored OCD-related and IAPS pictures) with an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (attentional distraction) contrasted with evaluation. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (evaluation > distraction; dampening of amygdala response during distraction) and unregulated viewing contrasts (OC > NE, AV > NE). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed (Talairach normalization, cluster correction) and ROI analyses; results are reported across groups with figures and supplementary tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli and whole-brain ICA/voxelwise results (I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11 satisfied), it does NOT instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/distancing/acceptance or instructions to dampen/amplify emotion). The task involved performing a two-back working memory task with angry and neutral faces rather than explicit emotion regulation. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (regulated-emotion task instruction) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Reappraisal vs Maintain) using visual IAPS images, meeting the review objective. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (Reappraise > Maintain; Maintain > Reappraise) and unregulated viewing contrasts, and conducts group-level, whole-brain mixed-effects voxelwise analyses with MNI peak coordinates (Z>2.3, p<.05). The sample includes a clinical population with a waiting-list control group (between-group comparisons are reported, and within-task effects are presented). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, not an empathy/perspective-taking paradigm).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs attend), using visual sad images (IAPS and normed photos). Participants include remitted MDD and healthy controls with separate group results. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraise-sad > attend-sad) and describes group-level voxelwise whole-brain GLMs with peak coordinates/cluster tables and figures in standard space. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-task effects). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and should be included.

This study is not a task-based emotion regulation fMRI study. It reports diffusion MRI (DTI) and resting-state fMRI effective connectivity (spectral DCM) in MDD and controls; subjects were scanned at rest with eyes closed and no stimuli or regulation instructions. Therefore it lacks any task, instructed emotion-regulation paradigm, visual emotional stimuli, within-task regulation or viewing contrasts, and any whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 — the paper reports only resting-state/effective connectivity and structural (DTI) analyses without any whole-brain task activation map. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I8 — sample includes patients and control group reported separately. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation task), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I9 (within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), and I10 (whole-brain task-evoked group-level activation). Full text appears complete (contains intro, methods, results, discussion). Conclusion: EXCLUDED because it does not address the review’s task-based emotion regulation fMRI inclusion criteria.

Exclusion reason: Study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps or reported peak coordinates; therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli - IAPS images), I8 (sample includes clinical and control groups), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrast to negative pictures). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy; task involves passive viewing with attention, not reappraisal or other instructed regulation), I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level statistical maps with peak coordinates reported). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This full text meets all required inclusion criteria for the review. It is an empirical, task-based fMRI study (I5) using an instructed emotion-regulation paradigm (cognitive reappraisal/‘Suppress’ vs ‘Maintain’; I6). Emotional stimuli were visual IAPS pictures (I7). The sample includes clinical groups and healthy controls with group-level results reported separately (I8). The analyses include within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (Maintain>Observe; Suppress>Maintain; I9). The paper describes whole-brain voxel-wise analyses in MNI space with results reported (text/figures and Supplementary Tables S1–S7), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I10) and acceptable reporting in supplementary material (I11). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes task activations). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This task-based fMRI study (EFNBACK) used visual emotional face distractors and instructed participants to ignore those distractors while performing a WM task, which constitutes an instructed cognitive-control/regulation demand. The paper reports within-task contrasts of emotional distractors (fearful > neutral) and WM-by-emotion interactions, and conducts whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with cluster-correction. Both patient (SZ) and healthy control groups are reported separately. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis criteria for task-based fMRI, instructed cognitive control of emotional responses, visual stimuli, eligible sample reporting, appropriate within-task contrasts, whole-brain analyses, and acceptable reporting of results.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation (dynamic faces) using visual emotional stimuli and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (emotions vs. shapes). It includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported significant clusters (right IFG and others) in standard space, and provides full methods, results and discussion. The sample (youth with BD, non-BD clinical, and healthy controls) is appropriate and reported separately. Although participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal instruction), the review objective accepts unregulated viewing contrasts; therefore the study is eligible. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because the regulated emotional stimuli are somatosensory (anticipation of electrical pain) rather than visual emotional stimuli required by the review. While the experiment uses visual countdown cues, the core emotional stimulus is pain anticipation/pain delivery (non-visual), so it fails inclusion criterion I7. The full text is complete and the study meets other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive reappraisal during anticipation), I8 (acceptable sample), I9 (reports within-task regulation contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), and I11 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (visual emotional stimuli).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study with whole-brain voxelwise analyses (satisfies I5, I9, I10, I11) and an eligible sample (I8). However, it does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met) and the emotional stimuli are word cues displayed on screen (‘safe’ and ‘shock’), i.e. word/sentence stimuli which the review’s criteria exclude (I7 not met). Therefore it fails to meet all required inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis and is excluded.

Excluded because the emotional stimuli regulated in the fMRI task are participant-generated negative self-belief sentences presented as text (word/sentence stimuli), not visual images or film; therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli requirement). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation—reappraisal), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports within-task regulation contrasts such as reappraise > react), I10 (reports whole-brain analyses/supplemental whole-brain results), and I11 (whole-brain results reported in supplements/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (stimuli are non-visual text/sentences). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (distancing) delivered socially by a psychotherapist, using visual IAPS images to elicit negative emotion in healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Social-Reg > Social-Look) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates and cluster-corrected results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not empathy-without-regulation). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study is excluded because it does not involve regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli (inclusion criterion I7 not met). This fMRI task contrasted a mindfulness meditation (acceptance-style instruction) with a distractor task (random number generation) without presenting emotional visual stimuli; although it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), instructs an emotion-regulation-related strategy (acceptance/mindfulness, I6), reports within-task contrasts related to the instructed meditation (I9), includes appropriate participant groups (I8), and provides whole-brain group-level activation maps with coordinates (I10,I11), it fails the key requirement that the regulated stimuli be visual emotional images or videos. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis objective focused on regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli.

Excluded because the study reports only ROI/SVC-corrected task activation results (amygdala SVC and other SVCs) and connectivity analyses, without a group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map. Exclusion criterion met: E4 (ONLY ROI/SVC results or partial coverage with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation—down-regulation), I7 (visual stimuli—aversive pictures), I9 (within-task contrast reported: regulate>view), I11 (coordinates reported in text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map reported). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes an instructed emotion-regulation condition (affect labeling) and an unregulated viewing condition (affect matching). Stimuli are visual (static facial expressions). The sample includes clinical (methamphetamine-dependent) and control groups with results reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts (affect label vs affect match; affect match vs shape match) and provides group-level whole-brain task activation results (e.g., affect match > shape match reported with peak coordinates in Table 4), not limited to ROI-only analyses. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is present. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all specified inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Decrease) versus viewing (Look) using visual static images (IAPS and NAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (Decrease vs Look and parametric modulation by stimulus intensity), and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates and thresholds. Although the paper also includes resting-state effective connectivity (spDCM) analyses, it additionally provides whole-brain task activation maps, so it does not meet exclusion criteria for reporting only connectivity/resting-state results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided content appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (‘Reframe’ = cognitive reappraisal) during presentation of visual stimuli (12 s video clips), satisfying the core intervention and stimulus requirements. Participants are clinical (generalized SAD) and the paper reports within-task contrasts (react vs. asterisk, reappraise vs. asterisk, and reappraise vs. react) and pre-to-post changes related to regulation. Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were conducted (maps converted to Talairach space, clusterwise correction applied) and results are reported at the group level (brain regions and cluster findings described; figures/tables/supplement likely contain peak coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; includes task activation maps; not only connectivity; includes within-task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation in older adults, it does not meet the stimulus-type inclusion criterion. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: worry induction and explicit worry suppression), I8 (sample qualifies: older adults with separate control group), I9 (reports within-task contrasts, e.g. WI–RS and WS–RS), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported MNI coordinates), I11 (results reported in text/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (emotional stimuli are NOT standard visual images/films but personalized sentences/script-driven worry prompts and imagery; the review excludes studies whose regulated stimuli are word/sentence stimuli or script-driven imagery with no visual stimulus). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) from the review’s list apply. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing I7.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (silent film clips) with clinical (IPV-PTSD) and healthy control groups. The paper reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (menacing > neutral; prosocial > neutral) and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster thresholds and peak results. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instructions were given (i.e. I6 not satisfied), the review’s scope allows unregulated viewing contrasts as eligible (I9), and the study therefore meets the meta-analysis objective. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed cognitive reappraisal using visual stimuli (IAPS/photographs) in children including a clinical (MDD-ever) and control group, and it reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > view sad). However, the analyses are ROI-based (Diekhof ROIs and amygdala subdivisions) and the paper does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) activation maps or peaks from a whole-brain analysis. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I10 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports ONLY region-of-interest results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I10. Exclusion criteria met: E4.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that meets all inclusion criteria: participants performed an instructed emotion-regulation task (reappraisal: REAL/PHOTO/LOOK) during fMRI (I5,I6), the regulated stimuli were visual static pictures (I7), both an unmedicated MDD group and healthy controls are reported separately (I8), within-task regulation contrasts are reported (e.g., negative/real vs negative/photo) (I9), and whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses with corrected clusters and peak coordinates are presented (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it is complete for screening purposes.

Exclusion criteria met: E4 (study reports only region-of-interest analyses with no accompanying whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps or peak coordinates). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: photographs of parent/stranger), I8 (sample includes children/adolescents), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrast: parent vs. stranger). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy — participants simply viewed images; no reappraise/distancing/other regulation instruction), I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results/coordinates reported). Because E4 is met (only ROI-focused results presented) and the required regulation instruction/whole-brain map criteria are not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample qualifies), I10 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses), and I11 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 — there is no instructed emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, acceptance, or other instructed modulation of emotional response); the manipulation is behavioral controllability of an aversive stimulus rather than an instructed regulation strategy. I7 — the emotional/aversive stimuli are auditory (tones and loud white-noise UCS), not VISUAL stimuli as required. I9 — the contrasts reported (e.g., CS+UCS vs. UCS alone; predictability × controllability) do not constitute an emotion-regulation contrast (e.g., reappraise > look) nor an unregulated visual viewing contrast. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED.

This task-based fMRI study uses visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports a within-task unregulated viewing contrast (faces > shapes). It includes group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses (SPM5) with reported region results and tables (MNI referenced) and used whole-brain analyses with small-volume correction for ROIs. Participants are an older adult clinical sample with nondepressed controls reported separately. Therefore it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrast), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with standard-space coordinates), and I11 (results presented in tables/figures). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to ignore emotional interference (an instructed cognitive control of emotional response), using visual emotional stimuli (angry face images). It reports within-task contrasts (angry face > gray square) and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (thresholds and coordinate tables/figures are provided). Sample (adolescents, clinical group and controls) is eligible. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; includes whole-brain activation maps; not only connectivity or only between-group contrasts; not an empathy/perspective-taking task). Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Accordingly, all relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive re-appraisal: 'Suppress' vs 'Maintain'), using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to the review (Maintain>Observe; Suppress>Maintain) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholds and MNI coordinates. The sample includes cocaine-dependent patients and a matched control group with separate within-group and between-group results. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). Therefore it satisfies I5–I11. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Given the clear reporting of task, visual stimuli, regulation contrasts, and whole-brain results, inclusion is appropriate.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual IAPS images with both Takotsubo patients and matched healthy controls, reports within-task contrasts (e.g., negative expected pictures vs neutral expected pictures), and performs whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses with coordinates/tables. Thus it meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. However, participants performed a passive emotional picture viewing/expectation task and were not instructed to use any emotion-regulation strategy (no instructed reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other cognitive regulation). Although the discussion addresses emotion regulation conceptually, no regulation instruction contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look) were implemented. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded.

This study is a resting-state, seed-based functional connectivity investigation with no task paradigm or instructed emotion-regulation manipulation. It therefore does not provide task-evoked within-task contrasts or whole-brain task activation maps required for the meta-analysis. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without task activation). Inclusion criterion I8 (sample eligibility) is met (adolescent female participants).
