This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed cognitive reappraisal (distancing) during stimulus presentation and included passive viewing, using visual IAPS images. It reports within-task regulation contrasts and long-term passive-viewing contrasts, presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and FWE correction, and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Sample is healthy adult participants. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Complete task-based fMRI study instructing cognitive reappraisal; regulation occurred during viewing of neutral faces (visual stimuli). Reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > look), whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with tables/figures and coordinates. Sample and methods are described in full text. Thus it meets all meta-analysis inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study (concurrent EEG/fMRI) that instructs emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal (cue ‘decrease’), with visual stimuli (IAPS images). Group-level fMRI GLM maps (NEU, NEG, NER) are reported with cluster correction and used to define ROIs, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. The paper reports within-task contrasts and condition-specific effects and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Sample includes healthy adult participants and group-level results are presented. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study using a visual emotional stimulus (a film clip) and an instructed regulation-style task (structured prompts to elaborate on an induced sad mood). The analysis includes within-task contrasts (elaboration vs. baseline/fixation), whole-brain, group-level voxelwise comparisons with thresholding and reported coordinates, and results are reported in text/tables. Participants are children (eligible sample). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is empirical, reports whole-brain task activation (not only ROI or connectivity), and includes within-task effects. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs a cognitive reappraisal strategy (Regulate vs Attend) to modulate responses to investment outcomes. The regulated stimuli are visual (market price displays/graphical feedback) that evoke emotional responses (regret/loss aversion) targeted by regulation. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing Regulate and Attend (behavioral and fMRI), and whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates in standard space. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal/emotional reappraisal strategies (emotion regulation) during a visual social-scenes task and during neurofeedback. Visual stimuli (social scenes images) were used. The sample (adolescent females) is eligible. The paper reports within-task activation contrasts (e.g., appraisal > fixation, reappraisal > fixation, reappraisal > appraisal) used as localizer contrasts, and describes group-level ROI probability maps with MNI coordinates for PFC and amygdala centers, indicating whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results in standard space. Thus all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met. No exclusion criteria are met.

This full-text reports an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (distancing/reinterpretation) using visual negative images (IAPS), includes clinical (MDD, BPD) and healthy control groups with group-level results reported separately, presents within-task contrasts related to regulation (Regulate>Maintain, Maintain>Observe), and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster/peak coordinates (TFCE, MNI). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material is referenced but not required for inclusion. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional images and reports whole-brain, group-level within-task contrasts contrasting negative vs. neutral images with peak coordinates. Although the task required emotion identification rather than an instructed emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/other regulation instruction), the review objective and inclusion criterion I9 permit unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., emotion > neutral). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and provides SPM whole-brain results and coordinates. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for inclusion as an unregulated viewing task-based fMRI study.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use a cognitive reappraisal (distancing) strategy while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS and photographs). Sample includes ages 6–23. Within-task contrasts (Reappraisal/Negative > Reactivity/Negative and related contrasts) are reported, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described with peak coordinates and tables. The paper also reports PPI connectivity analyses but not exclusively, and whole-brain activation maps and tables are provided. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables).

Full text reviewed and excluded because the emotional stimuli used are monetary gambles and outcomes (financial decision-making), not visual emotional stimuli such as static images or film/video. Therefore inclusion criterion I7 (emotional stimuli are VISUAL images or video) is not met. The study does satisfy: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation via reappraisal/perspective-taking), I8 (appropriate sample reporting), I9 (reports within-task regulation and viewing contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), and I11 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to upregulate positive-social emotions via self-referential imagination (an instructed regulation strategy). Stimuli are visual (IAPS/NAPS/GAPED photographs). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., upregulate positive > viewing neutral) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and coordinate reporting. All inclusion criteria relevant to the review are satisfied, and none of the exclusion criteria apply (the study reports whole-brain activation results in addition to DCM connectivity analyses). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (increase, decrease, maintain) while recalling previously encoded IAPS images. The emotional stimuli are visual (IAPS pictures encoded pre-scan), the sample is healthy young adults, and the paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., decrease>maintain, increase>maintain) and post-scan recognition. Analyses include group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistics normalized to MNI space with reported peak coordinates and tables; SVC was used for amygdala but whole-brain results are present. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to perform attention-shifting and an appraisal (like/dislike) task that functions as an instructed emotion-appraisal strategy. Stimuli are visual static composite images of faces and scenes. The paper reports within-task contrasts directly related to regulation (like/dislike – male/female; indoor/outdoor – male/female) and implicit emotion processing (male/female – face-only). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates (MNI) and FWE thresholds. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based, within-subject fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (film clips) and reports task-evoked whole-brain group analyses (GLM) with cluster results and coordinates (Tables/Figures). Although the study did not instruct an explicit regulation strategy (it probed implicit regulation), it reports unregulated viewing contrasts (negative vs neutral) and stimulation-related modulation of emotion-related activation, which fits the review objective to include studies that either instruct regulation or involve viewing without regulating. Sample and analyses meet eligibility: participants scanned during an emotion-induction task, visual stimuli (videos), whole-brain group results, and reported contrasts relevant to emotion processing. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, non-empirical) are violated.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of visual emotional stimuli that tests relationships among inattention, brain activity, and perceived stress, it does NOT meet the requirement that an emotion regulation strategy was instructed (I6). The task involved implicit processing (matching negative faces vs shapes) with no instruction to regulate; therefore there is no within-task instructed reappraisal contrast (e.g., “reappraise > look”). While the study provides a within-task unregulated viewing contrast (Match Faces > Match Shapes) and subject-level whole-brain maps used for pattern expression analyses, it does not report a traditional group-level whole-brain task-evoked regulation contrast with peak coordinates as required (I10 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (contains an unregulated viewing contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) appear to be met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (positive and minimizing reappraisal) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The sample is healthy adults, and the paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., positive reappraisal > natural response; minimizing reappraisal > natural response) and parametric analyses. Group-level whole-brain analyses and peak coordinates are reported (whole-brain contrasts, SVC and cluster-corrected results, and reported peaks in MNI space). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study in adolescents that includes both an instructed explicit emotion-regulation task (Perspective Task: ‘Far’ distancing/reappraisal vs ‘Close’) and an implicit regulation task (emotional N-Back). Stimuli are visual (faces, IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts indexing regulation and viewing (e.g., Far[Neg-Neu] > Close[Neg-Neu], 2-Back vs 0-Back contrasts) and describes whole-brain analyses (reported in supplement), satisfying the requirement for group-level whole-brain task activation maps. A clinical group (internalizing disorders) and a comparison group are reported separately. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; includes within-task effects). Full text is complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults that instructed participants to use emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and distraction) while viewing negative and neutral visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., view NEG – reappraise; view NEG – distract) and provides peak coordinates in standard MNI space. Although primary ROI/SVC results are emphasized, the manuscript states complementary whole-brain exploratory analyses are provided in the supplementary material (with coordinates), satisfying the requirement for group-level whole-brain task activation reporting. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the article is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of passive viewing of emotional faces (meets I5). Stimuli are visual (I7), samples include patients and controls reported separately (I8), and the paper reports unregulated viewing contrasts (negative faces > baseline) with coordinates (I9, I11). However, no instructed emotion-regulation task was used (I6 not met). Critically, all task-evoked activation analyses were performed within an anatomical mask (bilateral amygdala and prefrontal cortex) rather than as an unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise task activation map; the paper therefore reports only ROI/mask-limited voxelwise results with no accompanying whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (meets exclusion E4). Also I10 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map) is not satisfied. Therefore the study must be excluded per E4. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (I6) using visual stimuli (IAPS images; I7). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reapp Neg vs Look Neg) and behavioral reappraisal success (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with MNI peak coordinates and cluster thresholds (I10, I11). Participant sample information is provided (I8). Methods, results and discussion are present in the full text (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria apply.

Full text reports an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an instructed cognitive reappraisal paradigm (titles prompting reinterpretation) with visual IAPS stimuli. The methods describe first-level within-subject contrasts (IAPS2–IAPS1) identifying upward and downward reappraisal, and second-level, group-level voxelwise t tests comparing high- and low-Mach groups. Results list activation clusters across the brain (Table/Fig references and peak coordinates implied) and report SPM-based processing; thus whole-brain, group-level task activation maps are available. All inclusion criteria for the review are satisfied (task-based fMRI; instructed emotion regulation—reappraisal; visual stimuli; acceptable sample; within-task regulation contrasts; whole-brain evidence; reporting in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI/SVC results, only connectivity, non-empirical, or only between-group contrasts without within-task effects) are met. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore include in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) while participants view visual emotional images (IAPS and internet photos). It reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation conditions (e.g., REAP > ESUP, NAT vs REAP) and unregulated viewing, and presents group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space and statistical thresholds. Sample and methods are appropriate and full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-visual stimuli, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and distraction) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). Sample: healthy volunteers. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (reappraisal > view, distraction > view, reappraisal vs distraction) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with FDR-corrected thresholds and coordinate tables; functional connectivity (PPI) is also reported but task activations are primary. Full article includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly addresses the review objective. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation-like task — affect labeling — was used), I7 (visual stimuli: emotional face images), I8 (eligible participant sample reported), I9 (within-task contrast affect label > gender label reported), I10 (group-level, whole-brain analysis used to identify functional peaks for ROIs), I11 (peaks/ROIs and contrasts are described and reported in figures/tables). Whole-brain group-level contrasts (AL–GL) were used to define functional peaks and extract percent signal change for predictive analyses, indicating standard-space voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Based on these factors, the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study instructing emotion-regulation strategies (mindfulness and a CBT-style “reality checking” cognitive reappraisal) applied during anticipation and perception of negative/unknown visual IAPS pictures. The study reports within-task contrasts (e.g. exp ng>nt, per ng>nt), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster thresholds and coordinates, plus ROI results. Sample comprises healthy adult participants with between-group comparisons but also within-task effects. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This study is a resting-state fMRI investigation of intrinsic functional connectivity in mTBI; it does not include any task-based emotion regulation paradigm or visual emotional stimuli, nor does it report within-task contrasts or whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria requiring task-based fMRI with instructed emotion regulation and visual stimuli. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (increase, decrease, maintain) while participants view visual IAPS pictures. It reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (e.g. negative>neutral, increase>maintain, decrease>maintain) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI peak coordinates and tables. The sample comprises healthy adult participants and methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study instructing emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) while participants viewed visual negative images (Chinese Affective Picture System). It reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > watch; suppress > watch; watch-negative > watch-neutral) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported activations/coordinates; small-volume amygdala analyses supplement but whole-brain results are present. Sample and stimuli meet inclusion, and the full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects). Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an original, task-based fMRI experiment that instructs cognitive reappraisal (decrease) versus look conditions using visual stimuli (IAPS and child-appropriate images). The sample spans ages 10–22 (children, adolescents, young adults). Behavioral contrasts (look negative > look neutral; decrease negative > look negative) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise fMRI analyses are reported with thresholding and peak coordinates/tables, and figures illustrate activation maps. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task contrasts and whole-brain maps). Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion requirements.

This is a task-based fMRI study (n=42) that instructs emotion-regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) during anticipation (cue) and stimulus (target) phases using visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g. Target Reappraisal > Target Appraise; Cue Suppression > Cue Reappraisal) and presents group-level whole-brain, FWE-corrected voxelwise results with MNI coordinates and tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli (faces), an eligible sample (healthy adults), and reports whole-brain group-level task activation results (satisfies I5, I7, I8, I10, I11). However, the task does not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses (e.g., reappraise, suppress, or otherwise down-/up-regulate emotion). Instead, it is a cognitive control/response-inhibition task (cue to report the ‘actual’ or ‘opposite’ emotion) and examines correlations with self-reported habitual regulation. Therefore it does NOT meet I6 (an instructed emotion regulation strategy) and does not provide within-task contrasts that clearly reflect an instructed emotion-regulation manipulation (I9 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that instructed a mindfulness emotion-regulation strategy during anticipation and viewing of emotional visual stimuli (IAPS). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (negative>neutral; unknown>neutral), group-level whole-brain random-effects comparisons with coordinates and cluster tables, and ROI analyses. It therefore satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I5); instructed emotion regulation (mindfulness) during expectation and stimulus (I6); visual static images as stimuli (I7); eligible sample (healthy adults) (I8); within-task contrasts reported (I9); group-level whole-brain maps with coordinates (I10); and adequate reporting in tables/figures (I11). The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Regulate) and includes an unregulated viewing/maintenance condition (Maintain and Observe) using visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Maintain>Observe; Regulate>Maintain) and provides group-level activation results with peak coordinates (MNI) and one-sample activations used to generate masks; PPI analyses also used whole-brain masking. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs cognitive emotion regulation (self-distancing), using visual negative images (IAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts (CER vs NoCER; parametric aPE regressors) and describes whole-brain GLM preprocessing and voxelwise analyses (including coordinate-based ROI center x=26,y=6,z=-8 and supplementary aPE-related activation results), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Sample and stimulus criteria are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is a task-based fMRI experiment with visual stimuli (food images) and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain analyses, but it does not include an instructed emotion regulation strategy. Specifically: (a) Exclusion criteria met: none. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task contrasts/unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (reports whole-brain results), I11 (results reported in text/tables). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instruction to regulate emotion/cognitive reappraisal or other instructed regulation). The meta-analysis requires studies that include instructed emotion regulation tasks (or else meet all listed inclusion criteria); because this study manipulated taste (an incidental, non-instructed intervention) rather than instructing participants to reappraise or otherwise regulate their emotional responses, it does not satisfy I6 and therefore must be excluded. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and distraction) during presentation of visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts and univariate GLM results (age-by-condition interactions), MVPA searchlight and ROI analyses, and whole-brain voxelwise thresholding with reported peak regions in MNI space. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an affect-labeling emotion regulation task (Label > Observe contrasts), with visual stimuli (static face photographs). Participants are adolescent females. Analyses include within-task regulation contrasts (Label>Observe for negative and positive), whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses, and reported PPI (task-related) whole-brain regression results (clusters reported in tables/figures). Affect labeling is an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (implicit regulation), satisfying the review’s allowed adjacent strategies. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only without task maps, not non-empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly instructs cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal: increase, decrease, look) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (increase > look, look > decrease, increase > decrease), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps with peak coordinates in standard space (MNI/ICBM) and tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual facial stimuli in healthy participants and reports within-task contrasts (e.g. Sad>Shape, Anger>Shape), so it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), and I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrasts). However, the task is an implicit emotion-processing task with no instructed emotion regulation strategy (does not meet I6). Analyses are restricted to ACC ROI (ACC123 mask) using region-specific cluster thresholds rather than reporting a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates; thus it violates E4 (reports only ROI/small-volume-corrected results with no whole-brain analysis) and does not meet I10 (whole-brain evidence). Therefore the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a Label (affect-labeling) vs View paradigm with dynamic visual stimuli (videos of adolescent faces). The Label condition is an instructed affect-labeling task (an implicit regulation strategy) and is contrasted with View and Blur, providing within-task regulation-related contrasts (Label>View, Label>Blur) and unregulated viewing contrasts (View>Blur). Analyses include group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise maps (with thresholding and NeuroVault uploads), and results are reported in the text/tables. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an original, task-based fMRI study in which participants were explicitly instructed to regulate their emotional responses (disengage/view/engage) using cognitive reappraisal focused on social distancing. Stimuli are visual (IAPS and photographs of violent scenes). The study reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (disengage>view, engage>view, linear contrasts) and unregulated viewing contrasts (negative>neutral). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with MNI peak coordinates and detailed methods/results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using BOLD imaging and an event-related design. The task explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (reappraisal via distancing; 'suppress' vs 'maintain'), with visual IAPS images as stimuli. Participants are healthy volunteers and within-task contrasts related to regulation are reported (e.g., distance > look, look > distance), with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses in SPM2 and peak coordinates reported in MNI space; small-volume correction for the amygdala is supplementary. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This full text meets all review inclusion criteria: it reports a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs cognitive reappraisal as an emotion regulation strategy (I6) during presentation of visual stimuli (sad and neutral photographs) (I7). The sample includes adolescents (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., reappraise sad > view sad, and view sad > neutral) (I9). The authors conducted group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (corrected whole-brain false-positive rate; supplemental Tables S12–S14) consistent with reporting peak coordinates in a standard space (I10) and present these results in-text with supplemental tables (I11). No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), it is empirical original data, and within-task effects are provided. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore INCLUDE.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (faces) and an instructed task that requires cognitive control over automatic emotional action tendencies (incongruent > congruent contrast). The paper reports within-task contrasts indexing emotional control and provides whole-brain group-level analyses with peak coordinates and small-volume corrections. The sample (police recruits) is an eligible participant group. Although not a classical reappraisal paradigm, the study explicitly tests instructed cognitive control of emotional responses, which fits the review’s I6 formulation. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion-control task (approach-avoidance task) that requires participants to override automatic social-emotional action tendencies, which qualifies as instructed cognitive control of emotional responses. Emotional stimuli were visual (faces). The report includes within-task contrasts (affect-incongruent > affect-congruent) indexing regulation, and both whole-brain and ROI analyses are described with peak coordinates and corrected statistics. The sample is healthy adults and core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, etc.). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in which participants were instructed to use emotion-regulation strategies (compassion or reappraisal) while viewing visual images of suffering and neutral images. The sample is healthy adult participants. The authors report within-task contrasts (suffering > neutral during regulation) and conducted group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (e.g., Group × Redistribution Rank interaction identifying IPC) with corrected results and reported coordinates/tables (main text and supplemental material). The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria. The provided full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental material is referenced but not required for inclusion. Hence I include this study in the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs emotion-regulation strategies (feel, accept, analyze) and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results; however the emotional stimuli are script-driven recall of negative autobiographical memories cued by words, not visual stimuli (images or video). This fails inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion-regulation strategies, including acceptance/analyze), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task regulation contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates), I11 (results reported in text/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (visual stimuli). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs participants to regulate (decrease) their negative emotional responses (cognitive reappraisal/instructed regulation) to visual stimuli (IAPS images and photographs of stigmatized individuals). It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., decrease > attend) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and tables of activations. The sample is healthy adults and the methods, results, and discussion are provided in full. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or perspective-taking-only design). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and can be included in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed participants to regulate (reduce) their emotional responses to visual stimuli (IAPS and media images). It reports within-subject 'regulate > view' contrasts and uses group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space (SPM2). The sample (healthy adult females) is an eligible participant group. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based, empirical fMRI study that instructed participants to volitionally regulate emotional responses (up-regulation of anterior insula by recalling/imagining negative personal events) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (painful pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts (regulation > baseline), and whole-brain group-level activation results with MNI coordinates and corrected statistics. The sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. Resting-state and PPI analyses are present but task-based whole-brain activation maps are reported, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task effects, and regulation was explicitly instructed). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed an emotion regulation strategy (‘Enhance’ vs ‘Watch’) during stimulus presentation and used visual static image stimuli (EmoPicS). It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g. PosUp > PosWatch, NeuUp > NeuWatch) and includes both ROI and exploratory whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with thresholding and coordinate reporting (tables/NeuroVault references). The sample (healthy young adults) is acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material referenced but not required. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-group task effects; not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11) and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal to increase/decrease emotion while viewing visual IAPS pictures. The methods describe a GLM and group-level whole-brain mixed-effects analysis (FLAME), and report reappraisal-related contrasts (increase/decrease > view) with peak MNI coordinates and cluster-thresholding. Participants include younger and older adults. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI with an instructed emotion regulation task (cognitive reappraisal vs. attention deployment), uses visual IAPS images (negative scenes), adult healthy sample, reports within-task contrasts (CR>AD, AD>CR, amygdala contrasts), and provides group-level whole-brain GLM results (random-effects maps, cluster-corrected). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; includes whole-brain analyses in addition to ROI/connectivity). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This full text meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) during stimulus presentation (I6); stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7); the sample is healthy adult participants, reported clearly (I8); the analyses include within-task contrasts comparing Reappraise versus Maintain (I9); group-level whole-brain activation analyses are reported with thresholding and tables/figures of results (I10,I11). The paper also reports behavioral results and comprehensive methods, and includes activation tables and coordinates as well as whole-brain connectivity analyses. No exclusion criteria are met: the study does not report only ROI/SVC results, nor only connectivity without whole-brain activation maps, nor is it non-empirical. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplementary listings). Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive emotion regulation (self-distancing reappraisal) during exposure to visual negative images (IAPS). It reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation versus attend (e.g., Response: Distance > Attend; Prediction Error: Distance > Attend) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-FWE correction and figures/tables describing activations. Sample is healthy adult participants. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, acquisition, analysis), Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all specified inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and should be included.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (eligible sample: older adults, clinical and control groups reported separately), I9 (reports within-task contrasts: Grief > Neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with MNI coordinates), I11 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 — no instructed emotion regulation strategy (task required word-counting; participants were not instructed to reappraise, distance, accept, or otherwise regulate their emotions), I7 — regulated/viewed stimuli are words (idiographic grief-related words), and the protocol/exclusions state that the review excludes word/sentence stimuli. Exclusion IDs met: none. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude due to failure to satisfy I6 and I7.

This is a task-based, event-related fMRI study that instructs participants to apply cognitive reappraisal (guided creative, ordinary, objective descriptions) to visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., creative > ordinary, creative > objective) and trial-by-trial coupling with pleasantness ratings. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are described with cluster/FWE thresholds and coordinates; ROI and ROI-derived results are supplemental but whole-brain maps and peak coordinates are reported. Participants are healthy adults (college students). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11) and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the study does not meet the review's requirement for an instructed emotion-regulation task (I6 not met): participants were not instructed to regulate emotion (stimulation was used to implicitly facilitate regulation). In addition, the emotional stimuli are primarily written offers/messages (word/sentence stimuli), which the eligibility criteria exclude as non-visual stimulus materials (I7 not met). The study does meet several other inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), includes an appropriate sample (I8), reports within-task contrasts such as unfair>fair (unregulated viewing) (I9), and reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps with results described/tabulated (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to satisfy I6 and I7.

Exclusion rationale: E4 applies (study reports ROI and pattern-expression analyses without presenting a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study with single-trial GLM and stimulus-evoked estimates), I7 (visual stimuli: static anti-smoking images), I8 (sample acceptable: smokers), I9 (reports unregulated/viewing-derived trial-level stimulus > implicit baseline estimates used in analyses). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation; study examined spontaneous/uninstructed pattern expression rather than an instructed reappraise/down-regulate task), I10 (no reported whole-brain group-level task activation maps/coordinate tables). Full text appears complete and methods/results/discussion are present, but because the paper reports only ROI/pattern-based task analyses without accompanying whole-brain group activation maps, it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement and must be excluded under E4.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal of visual stimuli (IAPS images), with healthy adult participants. Within-task contrasts comparing reappraisal vs. natural viewing (ReappNeg vs LookNeg) are reported, and voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates are presented. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, stimuli, fMRI acquisition, analyses), Results, and Discussion; supplemental materials are noted but not required. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs a cognitive reappraisal strategy (distancing) during the anticipation/cue period of a visual reward task (coin images). Participants were healthy adults. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., regulate > permit, and permit > regulate interactions) and parametric modulation analyses relating neural activity to behavior. Group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses are reported with MNI coordinates and corrected thresholds; ROI results are also presented but are accompanied by whole-brain results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: the fMRI task did NOT instruct participants to regulate their emotional response. Participants performed a yes/no dating evaluation and derogation occurred implicitly; post-scan probe indicated they were not instructed or aware of regulating. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: static photographs), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports within-task contrasts related to regulation/unregulated viewing: reject>accept and attractiveness contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates reported), I11 (results reported in text/tables/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E7 violations). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Because the meta-analysis requires instructed emotion-regulation tasks, this implicit/unaasked regulation study must be excluded.

Full text is complete. The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual socioaffective stimuli (I5, I7). Sample includes adolescents (I8). Analyses report within-task contrasts tied to task conditions and a parametric modulator for successful vs. failed inhibition (interpreted as emotion-regulation-related effects) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with MNI coordinates (I9, I10, I11). However, the critical inclusion criterion I6 is not met: participants were instructed to perform a go/no-go distraction/inhibition task and were not instructed to use an explicit emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance) to up- or down-regulate their emotional responses. Instead, regulation was implicit/incidental to task demands. No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I6) and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to regulate (down-regulate) their emotional responses to visual stimuli (IAPS and media pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts (regulate negative > view negative; regulate positive > view positive) and group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with reported peak coordinates (MNI) and voxelwise thresholds. Participant sample and analyses meet inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-task effects, and is not an empathy-only task). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly examines instructed emotion regulation (NAT, cognitive reappraisal REAP, and expressive suppression ESUP). Stimuli are visual static images (IAPS and photographs). The sample (19 healthy adults) qualifies. The paper reports within-task contrasts and condition-specific effects (e.g., social pleasant vs nonsocial pleasant; social unpleasant vs nonsocial unpleasant across NAT, REAP, ESUP), and performs whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates and cluster maps. No exclusion criteria are met (not non-empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports within-task effects, and includes explicit regulation instructions). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I5–I11 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which children (8–10 y) were instructed to use a cognitive reappraisal/distancing strategy to suppress sadness elicited by visual film clips. The paper reports within-task contrasts (main effect of Regulation, Emotion×Regulation interaction) and provides group-level voxelwise results with MNI coordinates from whole-brain searches (and SVC), with methods, results, and discussion present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (task-based fMRI, instructed emotion regulation—reappraisal, visual stimuli—films, eligible sample, relevant within-task contrasts, and whole-brain peak coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (extrinsic/antecedent reappraisal via precedent descriptions), uses visual stimuli (static mutilation and neutral images), includes healthy adult participants, reports within-task contrasts (unpleasant>neutral in real and fictitious contexts; ROI paired t-tests showing attenuation), and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates after normalization. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing full assessment. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which adolescents were instructed to use cognitive reappraisal (decrease trials) while viewing visual negative images (IAPS and youth-normed pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts (decrease > look; look negative > look neutral) and analyses comparing runs before vs after a targeted rejection. Whole-brain group-level voxelwise results are reported with peak activations and cluster correction (coordinates/peaks in tables and figures). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, includes whole-brain activation maps, not only connectivity or ROI-only results, and includes within-group task effects).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal to regulate craving for visually presented food images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Regulate Craved > Look Craved; Look Craved > Look Not Craved) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster thresholds and coordinates. Sample (10–23 y females) is eligible. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; not connectivity-ONLY; reports within-group task effects; not an empathy/perspective-taking task).

This is a task-based fMRI study in which adolescents viewed visual food images and were instructed to use cognitive reappraisal and suppression strategies (costs of eating, benefits of not eating, suppress craving) versus an imagine-eating control. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., costs of eating > imagine eating) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with multiple-comparison correction. The stimuli are visual images, the regulation instructions qualify as cognitive reappraisal/controlled regulation, and results are reported at the whole-brain level. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive emotion regulation (positive reappraisal) during exposure to visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing Positive Reappraisal vs Negative Attend and other viewing contrasts, and whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses using FSL with cluster correction and supplemental tables/figures for results. The sample (clinical women with emotional distress disorders) is acceptable per criteria, and analyses include whole-brain maps and reported coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group effects, and involves instructed regulation rather than mere perspective-taking). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to generate cognitive reappraisals to downregulate anger (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy). The reappraisal task presents matching photographs (visual stimuli) during trials, satisfying the visual-stimuli requirement. The paper reports within-task contrasts (RGT vs baseline/fixation and RGT vs AUT) and whole-brain, voxelwise-corrected group analyses with reported activation clusters/coordinates. Sample and methods are appropriate and the full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion E4 applies: the neuroimaging group analyses were conducted within an a priori ROI mask (Harvard‐Oxford regions) and results are reported from ROI-restricted voxelwise tests; no whole-brain (unrestricted) group-level task activation map is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: food/object pictures), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (within-task contrasts reported: food>object during anticipation and rating), and I11 (peak coordinates and results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation/cognitive reappraisal or other regulation strategy was used—the task involved anticipation and pleasantness rating without regulation instructions) and I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task map). Therefore the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (increase, maintain, decrease) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (increase/decrease > maintain) and uses group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses with cluster correction. The sample (older adults) is eligible and analyses/contrasts relevant to emotion regulation are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not a review). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli with a suitable sample and reports an unregulated aversive>neutral anticipation contrast plus an exploratory whole-brain analysis with peak coordinates, it does NOT meet the key inclusion criterion I6: the task did not instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy. The study measured dispositional (self-reported) reappraisal and correlated it with neural activity, but there was no within-task, instructed regulation condition or contrast (e.g., reappraise > attend). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to decrease emotional responses using reappraisal (Decrease trials). Stimuli are visual (IAPS and other pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Decrease > Watch, Watch > Decrease, interaction contrasts) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space; results are described in the text. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I11.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to downregulate emotion using cognitive reappraisal while viewing visual IAPS pictures. The methods report within-task contrasts (decrease vs view), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with FWE cluster correction and reported coordinates/figures, and ROI analyses are supplementary. The participant sample (N=24 females) is eligible. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion downregulation using visual IAPS stimuli in unaffected relatives and controls; it reports within-task contrasts (downregulate > view) and ROI-based group comparisons. However, the full text presents only ROI-extracted BOLD results and subsequent ROI-based statistics and clustering; it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space in the manuscript text provided. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY region-of-interest results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level map/peak coordinates reported). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (faces) and reports whole-brain group-level analyses and within-task contrasts (condition > baseline). However, the experimental task is impression formation with no instruction to regulate emotional responses (no reappraisal, acceptance, distancing, or other instructed regulation). Thus inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy during the task) is not met. The study does meet I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (acceptable sample), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrasts / condition > baseline), I10 (whole-brain analyses), and I11 (results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria from the review (E3–E7) are triggered. Because one required inclusion criterion (I6) is not satisfied, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation using an emotion-label vs emotion-match task interpreted as implicit emotion regulation. Visual stimuli (facial images) were used. The paper reports within-task contrasts (label > match) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and cluster thresholds, and includes ROI and PPI analyses. Participants are early-adolescent males and females (eligible sample). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (inclusion criterion I6 not met). The study is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (faces) (I7), with an eligible sample (I8). It reports within-task contrasts for viewing emotional stimuli (fear > neutral; neutral+fear > control) consistent with unregulated viewing contrasts (I9), and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates/supplementary material (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not a review). Therefore it fails the requirement for instructed emotion regulation (I6) and is excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (colored squares) in a fear-conditioning paradigm and reports within-task contrasts (CS- > CS+ and CS+ > CS-) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise inference (FWE-corrected cluster results). Although no explicit emotion-regulation strategy was instructed, the meta-analysis objective allows inclusion of unregulated viewing/task contrasts; the study provides appropriate within-task affective contrasts and whole-brain coordinates/analytic details. The sample (n=32 healthy adults) meets participant criteria. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, not between-group-only, not an empathy/perspective-taking-only task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (attentional deployment) during stimulus presentation (I6); stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7); the sample is healthy adult participants with reported results (I8); the paper reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation (focus on arousing/non-arousing) to natural viewing (I9); group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates, tables, and cluster-level FWE correction (I10, I11). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, etc.).

This task-based fMRI study meets many inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9): it uses an instructed cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task during fMRI with visual stimuli (film clips), reports within-task contrasts (Regulate vs Attend), and includes adolescent/young-adult participants. However, the paper reports task activation results using ROI-based analyses rather than providing a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates in standard space. Although PPI connectivity results are reported with whole-brain coordinates, there is no whole-brain task activation map reported. This violates inclusion criterion I10 and falls under exclusion criterion E4 (only ROI/small-volume task results with no whole-brain analysis). Therefore the study is excluded.

Full text is complete. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation — cognitive reappraisal: UP/DOWN/distancing), I8 (sample acceptable; patient and control groups reported), I9 (within-task contrasts reported: UP-minus-M, DOWN-minus-M), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I11 (whole-brain results described/tabled). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (stimuli must be VISUAL). This study uses standardized negative scripts (verbal, script-driven imagery) as stimuli rather than visual images or film; regulated stimuli are non-visual, so it does not meet the meta-analysis stimulus criterion and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (naturalistic video clips) and reports within-task contrasts (negative > neutral, positive > neutral) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reported peak coordinates. The sample includes children and adults. Although participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy, the meta-analysis objective allows inclusion of unregulated viewing contrasts; the study therefore satisfies the review aim. The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Partial exclusion of a small portion of middle/superior temporal cortex from acquisition is noted but whole-brain analyses within the acquired volume are reported, so E4 does not apply.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli (faces), whole-brain group analyses, and relevant within-task contrasts, it does not meet the key requirement that an emotion regulation strategy be instructed. The paradigm instructs participants to label or match affect (affect labeling), which the authors characterize as incidental/implicit regulation, but participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I6 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample appropriate), I9 (within-task contrasts reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain maps), I11 (results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Because I6 (explicitly instructed emotion regulation) is not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Emotion Regulation Task: Reappraise Negative vs Look Negative) using visual stimuli (IAPS images). The sample includes clinical groups (MDD and SAD) which are acceptable. The analyses report within-task contrasts (Reappraise Negative > Look Negative) and whole-brain voxelwise regression results with peak coordinates in standard space. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

The full text describes a task-based fMRI study in which participants were instructed to use cognitive reappraisal (enhance/suppress/maintain) while viewing visual IAPS pictures. It reports within-task contrasts (suppress > maintain; enhance > maintain), performed voxelwise whole-brain analyses (PPI and group-level maps, cluster-thresholded across the whole brain), and provides group-level results and coordinates/tables. The sample (healthy adult males) is eligible. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only without whole-brain task maps, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a methods paper that includes an empirical fMRI example (social contact hand-holding) with task-based visual stimuli and within-task contrasts, but it does not meet key inclusion requirements. Exclusion IDs met: E4 (reports only ROI voxelwise analyses with no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task contrasts such as threat > baseline and condition comparisons). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy—participants experienced social contact rather than being instructed to reappraise or otherwise regulate), I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps with peak coordinates reported). Full text appears complete for screening (not truncated). Given E4 and failure to satisfy I6 and I10, exclude.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) with visual task stimuli (MID cues and targets) (I7), an eligible sample (adolescents) (I8), reporting within-task contrasts of anticipation/receipt (e.g., anticipation of loss vs no-incentive) that function as unregulated emotional-processing contrasts (I9), and it reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses with coordinates (I10,I11). However, the study does NOT instruct participants to use any emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other instructed regulation) during the task; the MID is a reward/loss task rather than an emotion-regulation paradigm, so Inclusion Criterion I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs cognitive reappraisal (Suppress) versus Maintain of negative affect elicited by visual IAPS pictures. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Suppress > Maintain, Maintain > Suppress) and regression analyses using subjective ratings, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects results with peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not an empathy-only perspective task). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and is eligible for inclusion.

The full text describes a task-based fMRI study in adolescents using visual IAPS images with explicit instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal: decrease/increase) and passive viewing. It reports within-task contrasts (look negative > neutral; decrease > look negative; increase > look positive), group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with cluster correction, and amygdala ROI analyses. Results and methods (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are fully present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in children that used visual stimuli (objects and fearful face images), performed whole-brain group analyses in Talairach space, and reported within-task contrasts comparing emotional contexts (Winning vs Recovery). Therefore it meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11. However, the study did not include any instructed emotion regulation strategy: participants were not instructed to reappraise, distance, accept, or otherwise intentionally regulate their emotional responses; the design induced emotions implicitly via point gain/loss and examined neural responses without explicit regulation instructions. Because inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion regulation strategy) is not met, the study must be excluded. Exclusion criteria triggered: none (E3–E7 not applicable).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs emotion regulation (cognitive downregulation/reappraisal) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (film clips). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Regulate vs Attend; Attend vs Neutral) and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and conjunctions, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of analyses. No exclusion criteria apply.

Meets inclusion criteria I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11: this is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (faces) (I7); participant groups (youth and healthy controls) are reported separately (I8); the paper reports within-task emotional contrasts (e.g., fear > neutral connectivity) and unregulated viewing contrasts (I9); exploratory whole-brain results/coordinates are reported in supplements (I10, I11). Does NOT meet I6: there is no instruction to participants to use an explicit emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, or other instructed regulation); the paradigm presents emotional distracters during an n-back task rather than directing participants to regulate their emotional responses. No exclusion criteria (E3-E7) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which participants were explicitly instructed to regulate (suppress) their emotional responses while viewing visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing suppression vs. baseline, presents whole-brain group-level analyses with coordinates and cluster tables, and includes behavioral and imaging results (activation and connectivity) relevant to instructed emotion regulation. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it is complete for screening purposes. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study presenting visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) and reporting task contrasts of negative > neutral (unregulated viewing). Participants include a clinical group (PMDD) and healthy controls. Data were preprocessed in MNI space and group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-corrected results and anatomical labels), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction (reappraisal/acceptance/etc.) was given (I6 not met), the meta-analysis objective explicitly allows studies that view visual emotional stimuli without regulation; thus the study provides the required within-task unregulated viewing contrasts and whole-brain maps for inclusion.

The full text is complete and clear. Meets several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion-regulation strategy: thought suppression/instructed cognitive control), I8 (acceptable sample: healthy adult participants), I9 (reports within-task regulation contrasts, e.g., Don't Think > Think), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates), and I11 (results reported in text/tables). However, it fails inclusion criterion I7: the emotional stimuli were script-driven imagery (participants imagined relationship scenarios) rather than externally presented VISUAL stimuli (pictures, faces, or film). The meta-analysis requires visual emotional stimuli; script-driven imagery is explicitly excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore EXCLUDE due to failure to meet I7 (non-visual stimuli).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal on visual stimuli in adolescents and reports within-task contrasts (meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). However, all voxelwise group analyses were constrained to a prefrontal cortex mask and the amygdala was analyzed with an ROI approach; no group-level, whole-brain (brain-wide voxelwise) activation maps or coordinates are reported. Therefore the study does not meet the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I10) and is excluded under E4 (reports only ROI/small-volume-corrected or partial-brain results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs Maintain) using visual stimuli (IAPS images). Participants are a clinical sample (anxiety and depression) reported at group level. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > Maintain) and whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space and cluster-correction; results are presented in text and figures. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply: this is empirical original data, not ROI-only or connectivity-only, and includes within-task effects. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI neurofeedback task in which participants were instructed to regulate positive-social emotions elicited by visual images (positive and neutral images), satisfying the emotion-regulation task requirement. The paper includes task-related results (behavioral learning, transfer-run activations) and reports group-level task activation peaks in MNI coordinates (e.g., dmPFC and left amygdala), indicating whole-brain task-evoked analyses. The stimuli are visual images, the sample is healthy adults, and within-task effects related to regulation and transfer runs are reported. Although the paper focuses on resting-state and effective-connectivity analyses, it presents within-task regulation-related contrasts and peak coordinates, meeting the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal/distancing, suppression, distraction) during visual stimulus presentation (IAPS pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing regulated vs. unregulated aversive conditions (e.g., Stim_RegAv>Stim_Av and reverse contrasts) and unregulated aversive vs. neutral. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates in MNI space and FWE-corrected maps; time-course plots and coordinates are provided. The sample (healthy adult females) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not an empathy perspective-taking without regulation). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (I7: IAPS pictures) in a healthy adult sample (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts of emotion versus neutral (e.g. NEG>NEU, POS>NEU) (I9) and describes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with standard thresholding and NeuroVault maps (I10, I11). However, the fMRI task does NOT instruct an explicit emotion regulation strategy (no reappraise/accept/other instructed regulation); it probes automatic/implicit emotion regulation during passive viewing, so it fails inclusion criterion I6. No exclusion criteria from the review (E3–E7) are met. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not satisfy I6 (instruction of an emotion regulation strategy), although it meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation strategies (Suppress-negative and Observe-negative/mindfulness), using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures), with a healthy adult sample. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Suppress-negative > Look-negative; Observe-negative > Look-negative) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space. Reporting of results includes tables/figures and coordinate peaks. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This full-text reports an event-related, task-based fMRI study in which participants were explicitly instructed to regulate emotion (detachment) versus permit naturally arising responses using visual stimuli (fear, disgust, neutral pictures). The sample (healthy female participants) is acceptable. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., permit > fixation, regulate > permit; comparisons of regulation effects) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates and FWE correction; coordinates and activation tables are described. Psycho-physiological interaction (connectivity) analyses are also reported but are accompanied by task activation maps. The manuscript includes full methods, results and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. Specifically, the fMRI task did not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing instruction)—participants passively focused on self-referential adjectives—so I6 is not met. Second, the emotional stimuli were words (adjectives) presented visually; the review excludes studies whose regulated stimuli are word/sentence stimuli, so I7 is not met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (eligible participant sample: adult groups), I9 (reports within-task contrasts of emotional > neutral: SC>NT and SP>NT), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction), and I11 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/supplement). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) with an eligible sample (I8) and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (I10, I11). However, it does NOT meet key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy — participants were not instructed to reappraise, accept, or otherwise regulate; the study examines spontaneous/implicit regulation), I7 (the emotional stimuli are interpersonal decision-making/negotiation offers and audio interactions rather than visual emotional stimuli such as static images or film clips), and I9 (no within-task contrast of instructed regulation vs. unregulated viewing such as “reappraise > look” — contrasts relate to offer fairness and gain-groups). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Because several required inclusion criteria are not met, the study must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy. Instead it used implicit facial-expression primes without any instruction to reappraise, accept, or otherwise regulate emotional responses.
